2.e: Kutsa a observing the action by which he bestowed b dravina

2.s: ayaṃ tanūnapādagnir asau hi tananāttanuḥ | tatastu madhyamo jajñe sthāne'yaṃ madhyamāttataḥ ||
2.d: अयं तनूनपादग्निर् असौ हि तननात्तनुः | ततस्तु मध्यमो जज्ञे स्थानेऽयं मध्यमात्ततः ||
2.e: This (terrestrial) Agni is Tanunapat (2). For that (celestial) Agni is tanu from tanana (extending): from him the middle (Agni) was born, then from the middle one, in (his proper) place, this (terrestrial) one.

2.s: anantarāṃ prajāmāhur napāditi kṛpaṇyavaḥ | napādamuṣya caivāyam agnistena tanūnapāt ||
2.d: अनन्तरां प्रजामाहुर् नपादिति कृपण्यवः | नपादमुष्य चैवायम् अग्निस्तेन तनूनपात् ||
2.e: The poets call an immediate a descendant (prajam) grandson (napat), and this (terrestrial) Agni is the grandson b of that (celestial) one; hence he is Tanunapat.

2.s: pṛthaktvena samāsaistu yajñe yacchasyate nṛbhiḥ | stuvantyāprīṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ||
2.d: पृथक्त्वेन समासैस्तु यज्ञे यच्छस्यते नृभिः | स्तुवन्त्याप्रीषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ||
2.e: Because he is individually (prthaktvena) lauded (sams) by men (nr) a combined at the sacrifice, therefore poets praise this (Agni) as Narasamsa (3) in Apri hymns.

2.s: punāti yadidaṃ viśvam evāgniḥ pārthivo'tha ca | vaikhānasarṣibhistena pavamāna iti stutaḥ ||
2.d: पुनाति यदिदं विश्वम् एवाग्निः पार्थिवोऽथ च | वैखानसर्षिभिस्तेन पवमान इति स्तुतः ||
2.e: And again because the terrestrial Agni purifies (punati) this universe, therefore he is praised by hermit seers as (the Purifier) Pavamana (4).

2.s: bhūtāni veda yajjāto jātavedātha kathyate | yaccaiṣa jātavidyo'bhūd vittaṃ jāto'dhivetti vā ||
2.d: भूतानि वेद यज्जातो जातवेदाथ कथ्यते | यच्चैष जातविद्योऽभूद् वित्तं जातोऽधिवेत्ति वा ||
2.e: There are thus five which correspond more or less to the five given in Nirukta vii. 19: three of these, jatavidya, jatavitta, jate jate vidyate, are followed by the second, third, and fourth in the above two slokas (30, 31), another, jatani veda, is partially followed by the first, while the fifth, jatani.. enam viduh, is followed by the second in i. 92 (jatair vidyate). [Note: The twenty-six names of Indra are (1) Vayu, (2) Varuna, (3) Rudra, (4) Indra, (5) Parjanya, (6) Brhaspati, (7) Brahmanaspati, (8) Ksetrasya pati, (9) Rta, (10) Vastospati, (11) Vacaspati, (12) Aditi, (13) Ka, (14) Yama, (15) Mitra, (16) Visvakarman, (17) Sarasvat, (18) Vena, (19) Manyu, (20) Asuniti, (21) Apam napat, (22) Dadhikra, (23) Dhatr, (24) Tarksya, (25) Pururavas, (26) Mrtyu] 7. The twenty-six names of Indra: Vayu, Varuna, Rudra, Indra.

2.s: vidyate sarvabhūtairhi yadvā jātaḥ punaḥ punaḥ | tenaiṣa madhyabhāgendro jātavedā iti stutaḥ ||
2.d: विद्यते सर्वभूतैर्हि यद्वा जातः पुनः पुनः | तेनैष मध्यभागेन्द्रो जातवेदा इति स्तुतः ||

2.s: aṇiṣṭha eṣa yattu trīn vyāpyaiko vyomni tiṣṭhati | tenainamṛṣayo'rcantaḥ karmaṇā vāyumabruvan ||
2.d: अणिष्ठ एष यत्तु त्रीन् व्याप्यैको व्योम्नि तिष्ठति | तेनैनमृषयोऽर्चन्तः कर्मणा वायुमब्रुवन् ||
2.e: But because he, in a most subtle form, abides in the air as the one pervading (vyapya) the three (worlds), the seers adoring (him) by reason of this function, called him Vayua (1).

2.s: trīṇīmānyāvṛṇotyeko mūrtena tu rasena yat | tayainaṃ varuṇaṃ śaktyā stutiṣvāhuḥ kṛpaṇyavaḥ ||
2.d: त्रीणीमान्यावृणोत्येको मूर्तेन तु रसेन यत् | तयैनं वरुणं शक्त्या स्तुतिष्वाहुः कृपण्यवः ||
2.e: But because with concrete moisture he alone covers (vrnoti) a these three (worlds), the singers in their praises speak of him, by reason of this faculty, as Varuna (2).

2.s: arododantarikṣe yad vidyudvṛṣṭiṃ dadannṛṇām | caturbhirṛṣibhistena rudra ityabhisaṃstutaḥ ||
2.d: अरोदोदन्तरिक्षे यद् विद्युद्वृष्टिं ददन्नृणाम् | चतुर्भिरृषिभिस्तेन रुद्र इत्यभिसंस्तुतः ||
2.e: Because he roared (arodit) a in the air, giving rain with lightning b to men, therefore he is highly praised by four seers c as Rudra (3).

2.s: caturvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇo bhūtvā vyavasthitaḥ | īṣṭe caivāsya sarvasya tenendra iti sa smṛtaḥ ||
2.d: चतुर्विधानां भूतानां प्राणो भूत्वा व्यवस्थितः | ईष्टे चैवास्य सर्वस्य तेनेन्द्र इति स स्मृतः ||
2.e: And having become the established (source of) life of the four kinds of beings, he rules (iste) over this universe; therefore he has been named Indra (4).

2.s: irāṃ dṛṇāti yatkāle marudbhiḥ sahito'mbare | raveṇa mahatā yuktas tenendramṛṣayo'bruvan ||
2.d: इरां दृणाति यत्काले मरुद्भिः सहितोऽम्बरे | रवेण महता युक्तस् तेनेन्द्रमृषयोऽब्रुवन् ||
2.e: Because he, associated with the Maruts, at the (proper) time bursts open (drnati) refreshment (iram) a in the sky, accompanied with great roar, therefore the seers called him Indra. - 1.

2.s: yadimāṃ prārjayatyeko rasenāmbarajena gām | kāle'triraurvaśaścarṣī tena parjanyamāhatuḥ ||
2.d: यदिमां प्रार्जयत्येको रसेनाम्बरजेन गाम् | कालेऽत्रिरौर्वशश्चर्षी तेन पर्जन्यमाहतुः ||
2.e: Because he alone endows (prarjayati) a this earth at the (proper) time with moisture produced from the sky, therefore the seers Atrib and the son of Urvasi (Vasistha) speak of him as Parjanya (5).

2.s: tarpayatyeṣa yallokāñ janyo janahitaśca yat | paro jetā janayitā yadvāgneyastato jagau ||
2.d: तर्पयत्येष यल्लोकाञ् जन्यो जनहितश्च यत् | परो जेता जनयिता यद्वाग्नेयस्ततो जगौ ||

2.s: bṛhantau pāti yallokāv eṣa dvau madhyamottamau | bṛhatā karmaṇā tena bṛhaspatiritīḻitaḥ ||
2.d: बृहन्तौ पाति यल्लोकाव् एष द्वौ मध्यमोत्तमौ | बृहता कर्मणा तेन बृहस्पतिरितीḻइतः ||

2.s: brahma vāg brahma satyaṃ ca brahma sarvamidaṃ jagat | pātāraṃ brahmaṇastena śaunahotra stuvañjagau ||
2.d: ब्रह्म वाग् ब्रह्म सत्यं च ब्रह्म सर्वमिदं जगत् | पातारं ब्रह्मणस्तेन शौनहोत्र स्तुवञ्जगौ ||

2.s: annaṃ kṣitibhyo vidadhad yadṛtuṣvaviśatkṣitau | tenainamāha kṣetrasya vāmadeva stuvanpatim ||
2.d: अन्नं क्षितिभ्यो विदधद् यदृतुष्वविशत्क्षितौ | तेनैनमाह क्षेत्रस्य वामदेव स्तुवन्पतिम् ||

2.s: manasemaṃ tu yaddṛśyaṃ madhyamaṃ lokamāśritam | śaṃsatsatyena satye vai sa eṣa stutavānṛtam ||
2.d: मनसेमं तु यद्दृश्यं मध्यमं लोकमाश्रितम् | शंसत्सत्येन सत्ये वै स एष स्तुतवानृतम् ||

2.s: raveṇāntārasaiḥ kṣiptai sthito vyomnyeṣa māyayā | ṛtasya śloka ityeṣa punaścainaṃ tato'bravīt ||
2.d: रवेणान्तारसैः क्षिप्तै स्थितो व्योम्न्येष मायया | ऋतस्य श्लोक इत्येष पुनश्चैनं ततोऽब्रवीत् ||
2.e: And by his magical power he abides in the air with internal moisture a shed with thunder: hence he (Vamadeva) again b spoke of him (as such in) 'the call of Rta' (rtasya slokah)c.

2.s: vāstuprayacchaṃllokasya madhyamaḥ sa tu pāti yat | tena vāstoṣpatiṃ prāha caturbhirimamaurvaśaḥ ||
2.d: वास्तुप्रयच्छंल्लोकस्य मध्यमः स तु पाति यत् | तेन वास्तोष्पतिं प्राह चतुर्भिरिममौर्वशः ||
2.e: But because (being in the) middle (sphere) he granting an abode (vastu) to the world, protects (it), therefore the son of Urvasi (Vasistha) proclaims him (to be) Vastospati (10) in four (formulas).

2.s: vācā vedā hyadhīyante vācā chandāṃsi tatra ha | atho vāk sarvamevedaṃ tena vācaspati stutaḥ ||
2.d: वाचा वेदा ह्यधीयन्ते वाचा छन्दांसि तत्र ह | अथो वाक् सर्वमेवेदं तेन वाचस्पति स्तुतः ||
2.e: Since the Vedas are learned with speech (vac), (and) the metres there (are recited) with speech, and moreover speech is this universe, therefore (he is) praised as 'Lord of Speech' (11). k.-This sloka (45) is

2.s: na kutaścana yaddīno vṛtvā tiṣṭhati madhyamaḥ | rāhūgaṇa ṛṣistena prāhainaṃ gotamo'ditim ||
2.d: न कुतश्चन यद्दीनो वृत्वा तिष्ठति मध्यमः | राहूगण ऋषिस्तेन प्राहैनं गोतमोऽदितिम् ||
2.e: And because he abides (in the) middle (sphere) surrounding (the world), not afflicted (dina) on any side, therefore the seer Rahugana Gotamab proclaims him as Aditi (12).

2.s: prajābhyastveṣa yaccharma kamicchanmanasā sukham | hiraṇyagarbhastenainam ṛṣirarcannuvāca kam ||
2.d: प्रजाभ्यस्त्वेष यच्छर्म कमिच्छन्मनसा सुखम् | हिरण्यगर्भस्तेनैनम् ऋषिरर्चन्नुवाच कम् ||
2.e: But because he is a protection to creatures, desiring (their) ka-happiness (sukha) a-in his heart, therefore the seer Hiranyagarbha, adoring (him), spoke of him as Ka (13).

2.s: iha prajāḥ prayacchansa saṃgṛhītvā prayāti ca | ṛṣirvivasvataḥ putraṃ tenāhainaṃ yamo yamam ||
2.d: इह प्रजाः प्रयच्छन्स संगृहीत्वा प्रयाति च | ऋषिर्विवस्वतः पुत्रं तेनाहैनं यमो यमम् ||
2.e: He giving (prayachan) offspring here, and gathering (them) goes forth (to the other world): therefore the seer Yamac calls him, the son of Vivasvat, Yama e (14).

2.s: mitrīkṛtya janā viśve yadimaṃ paryupāsate | mitra ityāha tenainaṃ viśvāmitra stuvansvayam ||
2.d: मित्रीकृत्य जना विश्वे यदिमं पर्युपासते | मित्र इत्याह तेनैनं विश्वामित्र स्तुवन्स्वयम् ||
2.e: Because all men making (mitrikrtya) a friend (of him) worship him, therefore Visvamitra a himself praising (him) calls him 'Mitra'b (15).

2.s: nidāghamāsātigame yadṛtenāvati kṣitim | viśvasya janayankarma viśvakarmaiṣa tena saḥ ||
2.d: निदाघमासातिगमे यदृतेनावति क्षितिम् | विश्वस्य जनयन्कर्म विश्वकर्मैष तेन सः ||
2.e: Because at the close of the hot months he refreshes the earth with water (rta), creating the activity (karma) of everything (visvasya), therefore he (is called) Visvakarman (16). nidaghamasatigame faziqatanfana m'r, faziatanfafaqa hd, fazraatanfana £k, faztuat- sanigame.

2.s: sarāṃsi ghṛtavantyasya santi lokeṣu yattriṣu | sarasvantamiti prāha vācaṃ prāhuḥ sarasvatīm ||
2.d: सरांसि घृतवन्त्यस्य सन्ति लोकेषु यत्त्रिषु | सरस्वन्तमिति प्राह वाचं प्राहुः सरस्वतीम् ||
2.e: Because he has lakes (saramsi) full of ghee in the three worlds, (the seer) a proclaims (him) as 'Sarasvat', (while) Vac (speech) they call Sarasvati.

2.s: prāṇabhūtastu bhūteṣu yadvenatyeṣu tiṣṭhati | tenainaṃ venamāharṣir veno nāmeha bhārgavaḥ ||
2.d: प्राणभूतस्तु भूतेषु यद्वेनत्येषु तिष्ठति | तेनैनं वेनमाहर्षिर् वेनो नामेह भार्गवः ||
2.e: Because being their life (prana) he moves (venati)abides in them, therefore the seer named Vena Bhargava b here calls him Vena (18).

2.s: sasṛje māsi māsyenam abhimatya tapo'grajam | tenainaṃ manyurityāha manyureva tu tāpasaḥ ||
2.d: ससृजे मासि मास्येनम् अभिमत्य तपोऽग्रजम् | तेनैनं मन्युरित्याह मन्युरेव तु तापसः ||
2.e: Primaeval (agraja) Heat (tapas), desiring (abhimatya), created him month after month: therefore Manyu Tapasa calls him

2.s: yadantakāla bhūtānām eka eva nayatyasūn | tenāsunītirukto'yaṃ stuvatā śrutabandhunā ||
2.d: यदन्तकाल भूतानाम् एक एव नयत्यसून् | तेनासुनीतिरुक्तोऽयं स्तुवता श्रुतबन्धुना ||
2.e: Because at the time when beings die he alone leads (nayati) (their) spirits (asun), therefore he is spoken of as Asuniti (20) by Srutabandhub who praises (him).

2.s: nidāghamāsātigame janma madhye bhavatyapām | naptāramāha tenainam ṛṣirgṛtsamada stuvan ||
2.d: निदाघमासातिगमे जन्म मध्ये भवत्यपाम् | नप्तारमाह तेनैनम् ऋषिर्गृत्समद स्तुवन् ||
2.e: At the end of the hot months (his) birth takes place in (their) midst a therefore the seer Grtsamada (in) praising (him) calls him Child of Waters (21).

2.s: apāmambaragarbhaugham ādadhatso'ṣṭamāsikam | yatkrandatyasakṛnmadhye dadhikrāstena kathyate ||
2.d: अपामम्बरगर्भौघम् आदधत्सोऽष्टमासिकम् | यत्क्रन्दत्यसकृन्मध्ये दधिक्रास्तेन कथ्यते ||
2.e: Because supporting (a-dadhat) the mass of waters contained in the atmosphere a for eight months, he roars (krandati) frequently in (their) midst, therefore he is described as Dadhikra (22).

2.s: māsena saṃbhṛtaṃ garbhaṃ navamenātha māsikam | svayaṃ krandandadhātyurvyāṃ dhātetyṛgbhiḥ sa gīyate ||
2.d: मासेन संभृतं गर्भं नवमेनाथ मासिकम् | स्वयं क्रन्दन्दधात्युर्व्यां धातेत्यृग्भिः स गीयते ||
2.e: He then himself roaring deposits (dadhati) in the earth for a month, the germ developed in the ninth month: (therefore) he is sung in stanzas (of the Rg-veda) as 'Dhatr'a (23).

2.s: stīrṇe'ntarikṣe kṣiyati yadvā tūrṇaṃ kṣaratyasau | ariṣṭanemistārkṣyarṣis tārkṣyaṃ tenaivamuktavān ||
2.d: स्तीर्णेऽन्तरिक्षे क्षियति यद्वा तूर्णं क्षरत्यसौ | अरिष्टनेमिस्तार्क्ष्यर्षिस् तार्क्ष्यं तेनैवमुक्तवान् ||
2.e: In the wide (stirne) air he dwells (ksiyati) or he swiftly (turnam) glides (ksarati): therefore the seer Aristanemi Tarksya c has spoken of him thus as Tarksya (24).

2.s: ruvanvyomnyudayaṃ yāti kṛntatrādvisṛjannapaḥ | purūravasamāhainaṃ svavākyenoruvāsinī ||
2.d: रुवन्व्योम्न्युदयं याति कृन्तत्राद्विसृजन्नपः | पुरूरवसमाहैनं स्ववाक्येनोरुवासिनी ||
2.e: Roaring (ruvan) in the sky he proceeds to sunrise, discharging a the waters from the abyss (krntatrat)b: (therefore) Uruvasinic (i. e. Urvasi) calls him Pururavas (25) d in her own words e.

2.s: yattu pracyāvayanneti ghoṣeṇa mahatā mṛtam | tena mṛtyumimaṃ santaṃ stauti mṛtyuriti svayam ||
2.d: यत्तु प्रच्यावयन्नेति घोषेण महता मृतम् | तेन मृत्युमिमं सन्तं स्तौति मृत्युरिति स्वयम् ||
2.e: But because with great din he goes driving on the deceased (mrtam), therefore him, as being death (mrtyu), the youngest son of Yama, named Samkusuka, himself praises as 'Mrtyu' (26). Causing the darkness to disappear from the sun and Dawn to appear, r, - - 60.

2.s: nāmnā saṃkusuko nāma yamaputro jaghanyajaḥ | saṃvartayaṃstamaḥ sūryād uṣasaṃ ca pravartayan ||
2.d: नाम्ना संकुसुको नाम यमपुत्रो जघन्यजः | संवर्तयंस्तमः सूर्याद् उषसं च प्रवर्तयन् ||

2.s: udito bhāsayaṃllokān imāṃścaiṣa svaraśmibhiḥ | svayaṃ vasiṣṭhastenainam ṛṣirāha stuvanbhagam ||
2.d: उदितो भासयंल्लोकान् इमांश्चैष स्वरश्मिभिः | स्वयं वसिष्ठस्तेनैनम् ऋषिराह स्तुवन्भगम् ||

2.s: puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ | tenainamastautpūṣeti bharadvājastu pañcabhiḥ ||
2.d: पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः | तेनैनमस्तौत्पूषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पञ्चभिः ||
2.e: Nourishing (pusyan) he causes the earth to thrive, dispelling the darkness with his rays: therefore Bharadvaja praised, him as 'Pusan' (3) with five (hymns).

2.s: trīṇi bhānti rajāṃsyasya yatpadāni tu tejasā | tena medhātithiḥ prāha viṣṇumenaṃ trivikramam ||
2.d: त्रीणि भान्ति रजांस्यस्य यत्पदानि तु तेजसा | तेन मेधातिथिः प्राह विष्णुमेनं त्रिविक्रमम् ||
2.e: Because the three (trini) regions (rajamsi) shine with brilliance as his footsteps, therefore Medhatithi a pronounces him (to be) Visnu (4) of the three strides (trivikrama).

2.s: kṛtvā sāyaṃ pṛthagyāti bhūtebhyastamaso'tyaye | prakāśaṃ kiraṇaiḥ kurvaṃs tenainaṃ keśinaṃ viduḥ ||
2.d: कृत्वा सायं पृथग्याति भूतेभ्यस्तमसोऽत्यये | प्रकाशं किरणैः कुर्वंस् तेनैनं केशिनं विदुः ||
2.e: Because, after making a sojourn (sayam) apart, he goes, at the departure of darkness, making light (prakasam) for beings with his beams, therefore they regard him as (the Hairy) Kesin (5).

2.s: saṃpratyekaikaśastvenaṃ yanmanyante pṛthaṅnarāḥ | viśve viśvānarastena karmaṇā stutiṣu stutaḥ ||
2.d: संप्रत्येकैकशस्त्वेनं यन्मन्यन्ते पृथङ्नराः | विश्वे विश्वानरस्तेन कर्मणा स्तुतिषु स्तुतः ||
2.e: Because all men (visve narah) now singly (and) separately think a of him, by reason of this function he is praised in laudations as Visvanara (6).

2.s: vṛṣaiṣa kapilo bhūtvā yannākamadhirohati | vṛṣākapirasau tena viśvasmādindra uttaraḥ | raśmibhiḥ kampayanneti vṛṣā varṣiṣṭha eva saḥ ||
2.d: वृषैष कपिलो भूत्वा यन्नाकमधिरोहति | वृषाकपिरसौ तेन विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः | रश्मिभिः कम्पयन्नेति वृषा वर्षिष्ठ एव सः ||
2.e: Because having become a brown (kapila) bulla (vrsa), he mounts the firmament, therefore he is Vrsakapi (7), (in) 'Indra is above all' (Rg-veda x. 86); (or) this highest bull (vrsa) goes causing to waver (kampayan) with (his)

2.s: sāyāhnakāle bhūtāni svāpayannastameti yat | vṛṣākapirito vā syād iti mantreṣu dṛśyate ||
2.d: सायाह्नकाले भूतानि स्वापयन्नस्तमेति यत् | वृषाकपिरितो वा स्याद् इति मन्त्रेषु दृश्यते ||
2.e: (i. e.) because he goes home (astam) at eventide causing beings to sleep, (his name) Vrsakapi may be (derived) from this; for in the three formulas beginning 'the waste' (dhanva: Rg-veda x. 86. 20-22) in the hymn to Vrsakapi, he appears to be bidden c thus (iti) by Indra.

2.s: triṣu dhanveti hīndreṇa prayukto vāriṣākape | viṣṇāterviśatervā syād veveṣṭervyāptikarmaṇaḥ | viṣṇurnirucyate sūryaḥ sarvaṃ sarvāntaraśca yaḥ ||
2.d: त्रिषु धन्वेति हीन्द्रेण प्रयुक्तो वारिषाकपे | विष्णातेर्विशतेर्वा स्याद् वेवेष्टेर्व्याप्तिकर्मणः | विष्णुर्निरुच्यते सूर्यः सर्वं सर्वान्तरश्च यः ||
2.e: Visnua may be from (the root) vis (visnati) or vis (visati), (or) from vevis (vevesti), expressing pervasion: (he) is (thus) explained as the Sun who is everything and is contained in everything.

2.s: pañca ṣaḍviṃśatiścaiva yāni nāmāni sapta ca | samyagagnīndrasūryāṇāṃ tānyuktāni yathākramam ||
2.d: पञ्च षड्विंशतिश्चैव यानि नामानि सप्त च | सम्यगग्नीन्द्रसूर्याणां तान्युक्तानि यथाक्रमम् ||
2.e: The five, the twenty-six, and the seven names of Agni, Indra, and Surya (respectively), have (thus) been duly stated in succession.

2.s: naipātikānāṃ nāmnāṃ tu prāguktairnāmalakṣaṇaiḥ | saṃpannānāṃ pṛthaktvena parisaṃkhyā na vidyate ||
2.d: नैपातिकानां नाम्नां तु प्रागुक्तैर्नामलक्षणैः | संपन्नानां पृथक्त्वेन परिसंख्या न विद्यते ||
2.e: But of the incidental names, accompanied by the abovementioned b nominal characteristics (nama-laksanaih), a separate enumeration does not exist.

2.s: pārthivī madhyamā divyā vāgapi trividhā tu yā | tasyāḥ sūktāni nāmāni yathāsthānaṃ nibodhata ||
2.d: पार्थिवी मध्यमा दिव्या वागपि त्रिविधा तु या | तस्याः सूक्तानि नामानि यथास्थानं निबोधत ||
2.e: As to Speech (Vac) also, who is threefold as terrestrial, middle, (and) celestial, listen to (an account of) her hymns (and) names according to her sphere.

2.s: kṛtsnaṃ tu bhajate sūktam eṣā nadya stutā bhuvi | yadā cainaṃ bhajantyāpo yadā cauṣadhayo yadā ||
2.d: कृत्स्नं तु भजते सूक्तम् एषा नद्य स्तुता भुवि | यदा चैनं भजन्त्यापो यदा चौषधयो यदा ||
2.e: Now she owns the entire hymn when the rivers on earth, and when the waters, (and) when the plants, being praised, own it.

2.s: agnāyī nāmato'pyeṣā bhūtvāgneyeṣu keṣucit | stutā nipātamātreṇa tatra tatreha dṛśyate ||
2.d: अग्नायी नामतोऽप्येषा भूत्वाग्नेयेषु केषुचित् | स्तुता निपातमात्रेण तत्र तत्रेह दृश्यते ||
2.e: Also when she becomes Agnayi a by name, she appears here (in the Rg-veda) in various passages (tatra tatra) praised only incidentally in some (hymns) addressed to Agni.

2.s: madhye satyaditirvāk ca bhūtvā caiṣā sarasvatī | samagraṃ bhajate sūktaṃ tribhireva tu nāmabhiḥ ||
2.d: मध्ये सत्यदितिर्वाक् च भूत्वा चैषा सरस्वती | समग्रं भजते सूक्तं त्रिभिरेव तु नामभिः ||
2.e: When she, being Vaca in the middle (sphere), has become Aditi and Sarasvati, she owns the complete hymn under (these) three names only.

2.s: eṣaiva durgā bhūtvarcaṃ kṛtvā syātsūktabhāginī | tannāmāni yamīndrāṇī saramā romaśorvaśī | bhavatyagrayā sinīvālī rākā cānumatiḥ kuhūḥ ||
2.d: एषैव दुर्गा भूत्वर्चं कृत्वा स्यात्सूक्तभागिनी | तन्नामानि यमीन्द्राणी सरमा रोमशोर्वशी | भवत्यग्रया सिनीवाली राका चानुमतिः कुहूः ||
2.e: [She on becoming Durga (and) uttering a stanza may own (whole) hymn] b. Her (other)

2.s: gaurdhenurdevapatnyo'ghnyā pathyā svastiśca rodasī | naipātikāni ṛgbhāñji yeṣāṃ nāmāni kānicit ||
2.d: गौर्धेनुर्देवपत्न्योऽघ्न्या पथ्या स्वस्तिश्च रोदसी | नैपातिकानि ऋग्भाञ्जि येषां नामानि कानिचित् ||

2.s: yadā tu vāgbhavatyeṣā sūryāmuṃ lokamāśritā | tathā sūktamuṣā bhūtvā sūryā ca bhajate'khilam ||
2.d: यदा तु वाग्भवत्येषा सूर्यामुं लोकमाश्रिता | तथा सूक्तमुषा भूत्वा सूर्या च भजतेऽखिलम् ||
2.e: But when this Vac becomes Surya, she belongs to that (celestial) world: thus on becoming Usas as well as Surya, she owns the entire hymn.

2.s: vṛṣākapāyyṛcaṃ bhūtvā saraṇyūrdve ca te dhruvam | nipātamātraṃ bhajate dyuvacca pṛthivī satī ||
2.d: वृषाकपाय्यृचं भूत्वा सरण्यूर्द्वे च ते ध्रुवम् | निपातमात्रं भजते द्युवच्च पृथिवी सती ||
2.e: And when she becomes Vrsakapayi (and) Saranyu, these two undoubtedly (own) a stanza. And when she is Earth corresponding to Heaven (dyuvat), she only owns (a stanza) incidentally d dve ca te

2.s: sūryāmeva satīmetāṃ gaurīṃ vācaṃ sarasvatīm | paśyāmo vaiśvadeveṣu nipātenaiva kevalāḥ ||
2.d: सूर्यामेव सतीमेतां गौरीं वाचं सरस्वतीम् | पश्यामो वैश्वदेवेषु निपातेनैव केवलाः ||
2.e: We see that when this Vac is Surya, Gauria, Sarasvati, they (are) in the hymns to the All-gods (praised) incidentally only.

2.s: ghoṣā godhā viśvavārā apālopaniṣanniṣat | brahmajāyā jahūrnāma agastyasya svasāditiḥ ||
2.d: घोषा गोधा विश्ववारा अपालोपनिषन्निषत् | ब्रह्मजाया जहूर्नाम अगस्त्यस्य स्वसादितिः ||
2.e: Ghosa, Godha, Visvavara, Apala, Upanisad, Nisade, Brahmajaya (who is) named Juhuf, the sister of

2.s: indrāṇī cendramātā ca saramā romaśorvaśī | lopāmudrā ca nadyaśca yamī nārī ca śaśvatī ||
2.d: इन्द्राणी चेन्द्रमाता च सरमा रोमशोर्वशी | लोपामुद्रा च नद्यश्च यमी नारी च शश्वती ||

2.s: śrīrlākṣā sārparājñī vāk śraddhā medhā ca dakṣiṇā | rātrī sūryā ca sāvitrī brahmavādinya īritāḥ ||
2.d: श्रीर्लाक्षा सार्पराज्ञी वाक् श्रद्धा मेधा च दक्षिणा | रात्री सूर्या च सावित्री ब्रह्मवादिन्य ईरिताः ||
2.e: Sri, Laksa, Sarparajnic, Vacd, Sraddha e, Medhaf, Sraddhae, Daksina, Ratri h, and Surya Savitrii, (all these) are pronounced to be female seers (brahmavadinyah).

2.s: navakaḥ prathamastvāsāṃ vargastuṣṭāva devatāḥ | ṛṣibhirdevatābhiśca samūde madhyamo gaṇaḥ ||
2.d: नवकः प्रथमस्त्वासां वर्गस्तुष्टाव देवताः | ऋषिभिर्देवताभिश्च समूदे मध्यमो गणः ||
2.e: The first group of these, consisting of nine, praised the deities; the middle series b conversed with seers and deities.

2.s: ātmano bhāvavṛttāni jagau vargastathottamaḥ | uttamasya tu vargasya ya ṛṣiḥ saiva devatā ||
2.d: आत्मनो भाववृत्तानि जगौ वर्गस्तथोत्तमः | उत्तमस्य तु वर्गस्य य ऋषिः सैव देवता ||
2.e: So the last group sang of the evolutionary forms (bhava-, vrttani) a of Self. Whoever is the seer (of a hymn by one) of the last group is also the deity.

2.s: ātmānamastaudvargastu devatāṃ yastathottamaḥ | tasmādātmastaveṣu syād ya ṛṣiḥ saiva devatā ||
2.d: आत्मानमस्तौद्वर्गस्तु देवतां यस्तथोत्तमः | तस्मादात्मस्तवेषु स्याद् य ऋषिः सैव देवता ||
2.e: Now (each seer of) the last group thus praised herself as the deity: therefore whoever may be the seer in self-laudations is at the same time the deity.

2.s: saṃvādeṣvāha vākyaṃ yaḥ sa tu tasminbhavedṛṣiḥ | yastenocyeta vākyena devatā tatra sā bhavet ||
2.d: संवादेष्वाह वाक्यं यः स तु तस्मिन्भवेदृषिः | यस्तेनोच्येत वाक्येन देवता तत्र सा भवेत् ||
2.e: He who utters the speech in colloquies should be (regarded as) the seer a in it; whoever may be addressed by that speech should be (regarded as) the deity therein.

2.s: uccāvaceṣu cārtheṣu nipātāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ | karmopasaṃgrahārthe ca kvaciccaupamyakāraṇāt ||
2.d: उच्चावचेषु चार्थेषु निपाताः समुदाहृताः | कर्मोपसंग्रहार्थे च क्वचिच्चौपम्यकारणात् ||

2.s: ūnānāṃ pūraṇārthā vā pādānāmapare kvacit | mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu pūraṇārthāstvanarthakāḥ ||
2.d: ऊनानां पूरणार्था वा पादानामपरे क्वचित् | मिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु पूरणार्थास्त्वनर्थकाः ||
2.e: Others again (are) occasionally (used) for the purpose of filling up a defective verses (pada). Those (particles) which in metrical books have the purpose of filling up (the verse) are meaningless

2.s: kamīmidviti vijñeyā ye tvanekārthakāśca te | iva na cinnu catvāra upamārthā bhavanti te ||
2.d: कमीमिद्विति विज्ञेया ये त्वनेकार्थकाश्च ते | इव न चिन्नु चत्वार उपमार्था भवन्ति ते ||

2.s: upamārthe nakārastu kvacideva nipātyate | mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu pratiṣedhe tvanalpaśaḥ ||
2.d: उपमार्थे नकारस्तु क्वचिदेव निपात्यते | मिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु प्रतिषेधे त्वनल्पशः ||
2.e: Now na is, in metrical books, only occasionally used as a particle (nipatyate) in the sense of comparison, but frequently in (the sense of) negation.

2.s: iyanta iti saṃkhyānaṃ nipātānāṃ na vidyate | vaśātprakaraṇasyaite nipātyante pade pade ||
2.d: इयन्त इति संख्यानं निपातानां न विद्यते | वशात्प्रकरणस्यैते निपात्यन्ते पदे पदे ||
2.e: There does not exist an enumeration of the particles (stating explicitly) 'there are so many'a. These particles are used (nipatyante) at every turn (pade pade) on account of the subject-matter (prakarana).

2.s: upasargāstu vijñeyāḥ kriyāyogena viṃśatiḥ | vivecayanti te hyarthaṃ nāmākhyātavibhaktiṣu ||
2.d: उपसर्गास्तु विज्ञेयाः क्रियायोगेन विंशतिः | विवेचयन्ति ते ह्यर्थं नामाख्यातविभक्तिषु ||
2.e: The twenty a prepositions (upasargah) are to be recognized by reason of their connexion with (verbal) action; for they differentiate the meaning in the inflexions of noun and verb.

2.s: adya śradantarityetān ācāryaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ | upasargān kriyāyogān mene te tu trayo'dhikāḥ ||
2.d: अद्य श्रदन्तरित्येतान् आचार्यः शाकटायनः | उपसर्गान् क्रियायोगान् मेने ते तु त्रयोऽधिकाः ||
2.e: Achaa, srad, antar-these the teacher Sakatayana considered prepositions because of their connexion with action; they are three more. anu all MSS. and r.

2.s: trīṇyeva loke liṅgāni pumān strī ca napuṃsakam | nāmasūktaprayogeṣu vācyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tathā ||
2.d: त्रीण्येव लोके लिङ्गानि पुमान् स्त्री च नपुंसकम् | नामसूक्तप्रयोगेषु वाच्यं प्रकरणं तथा ||
2.e: There are just the three genders in popular usage (loke)masculine, feminine, neuter. In (regard to) nouns, the employment of which has been stated, the subject-matter must be stated in this way.

2.s: teṣāṃ tu nāmabhirliṅgair grahaṇaṃ sarvanāmabhiḥ | kṛtākṛtasya sadṛśo gṛhītasya punargrahaḥ ||
2.d: तेषां तु नामभिर्लिङ्गैर् ग्रहणं सर्वनामभिः | कृताकृतस्य सदृशो गृहीतस्य पुनर्ग्रहः ||
2.e: Now these (names) are mentioned (not only) by means of nouns, (but also) by means of genders; by means of pronouns repeated mention (is made) of (a noun already) mentioned, similar to (the repeated mention of) a positive or negative act (krtakrtasya)a.

2.s: pādasūktaṛgardharcanāmānyanyāni yāni ca | sarve nāmāni caivāhura anye caivaṃ yathā kathā ||
2.d: पादसूक्तऋगर्धर्चनामान्यन्यानि यानि च | सर्वे नामानि चैवाहुर अन्ये चैवं यथा कथा ||
2.e: All (authorities) say that the names (occurring) in verses, hymns, stanzas, hemistichs, and any others (there may be), (are) nouns; some (call them) so according to circumstances (yatha katha).

2.s: pradhānamarthaḥ śabdo hi tadguṇāyatta iṣyate | tasmānnānānvayopāyaiḥ śabdānarthavaśaṃ nayet ||
2.d: प्रधानमर्थः शब्दो हि तद्गुणायत्त इष्यते | तस्मान्नानान्वयोपायैः शब्दानर्थवशं नयेत् ||
2.e: The sense is the chief thing; for a term (sabda) is required (to be) dependent on the qualities (guna) of it (the 60 sense); therefore one should bring terms under subjection to the sense by the various expedients of construing.

2.s: atiriktaṃ padaṃ tyājyaṃ hīnaṃ vākye niveśayet | viprakṛṣṭaṃ ca saṃdadhyād ānupūrvīṃ ca kalpayet ||
2.d: अतिरिक्तं पदं त्याज्यं हीनं वाक्ये निवेशयेत् | विप्रकृष्टं च संदध्याद् आनुपूर्वीं च कल्पयेत् ||
2.e: A redundant word (pada) should be rejected, while one that is lacking one should introduce into the sentence; and one that is far removed one should bring into juxtaposition, and should (then) arrange the regular sequence (of the words ).

2.s: liṅgaṃ dhātuṃ vibhaktiṃ ca saṃnamettatra tatra ca | yadyatsyācchāndasaṃ mantre tattatkuryāttu laukikam ||
2.d: लिङ्गं धातुं विभक्तिं च संनमेत्तत्र तत्र च | यद्यत्स्याच्छान्दसं मन्त्रे तत्तत्कुर्यात्तु लौकिकम् ||
2.e: Gender, root, and inflexion one should, in their respective places, adapt (to the sense). Whatever is Vedic in a formula one should turn into everyday speech (laukika). dhatum vibhakti m.

2.s: yāvatāmeva dhātūnāṃ liṅgaṃ rūḍhigataṃ bhavet | arthaścāpyabhidheyaḥ syāt tāvadbhirguṇavigrahaḥ ||
2.d: यावतामेव धातूनां लिङ्गं रूढिगतं भवेत् | अर्थश्चाप्यभिधेयः स्यात् तावद्भिर्गुणविग्रहः ||
2.e: The analysis of the secondary elements (guna) a may be (effected) by the aid of all roots (dhatu) which possess a traditional characteristic form (linga), and the sense of which can be stated.

2.s: dhātūpasargāvayavaguṇaśabdaṃ dvidhātujam | bahvekadhātujaṃ vāpi padaṃ nirvācyalakṣaṇam ||
2.d: धातूपसर्गावयवगुणशब्दं द्विधातुजम् | बह्वेकधातुजं वापि पदं निर्वाच्यलक्षणम् ||
2.e: A word (pada), the definition of which can be expressed, whether it be derived from two roots, many (roots ), or one root, is one consisting of a sound (sabda) that contains root, preposition, members (avayava), and secondary elements (guna).

2.s: dhātujaṃ dhātujājjātaṃ samastārthajameva vā | vākyajaṃ vyatikīrṇaṃ ca nirvācyaṃ pañcadhā padam ||
2.d: धातुजं धातुजाज्जातं समस्तार्थजमेव वा | वाक्यजं व्यतिकीर्णं च निर्वाच्यं पञ्चधा पदम् ||
2.e: A word may be explained in five ways, (viz.) as derived from a root, as derived from the derivative a of a root, as derived from a compound meaning (samastartha), as derived from a sentence (vakya), and as (of) confusedd (derivation). a Corresponding to taddhita below, 106, and Nirukta ii. 2. with a samasanta suffix; cp. taddhita-samasesu, Nirukta ii. 2. itihasa (=iti haasa). ii. I: ady-anta-viparyayah.

2.s: dvigurdvandvo'vyayībhāvaḥ karmadhāraya eva ca | pañcamastu bahuvrīhiḥ ṣaṣṭhastatpuruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
2.d: द्विगुर्द्वन्द्वोऽव्ययीभावः कर्मधारय एव च | पञ्चमस्तु बहुव्रीहिः षष्ठस्तत्पुरुषः स्मृतः ||
2.e: Dvigu, Dvandva, Avyayibhava, and Karmadharaya, the fifth Bahuvrihi, and the sixth called Tatpurusa (are the compounds). * This sloka is quoted by Durga on Nirukta ii. 2. Only four classes are distinguished in the Vajasaneyi Samhita Pratisakhya (i. 27 and v. I, commentary), which does not mention the dvigu or the karmadharaya class.

2.s: vigrahānnirvacaḥ kāryaṃ samāseṣvapi taddhite | pravibhajyaiva nirbhūyād daṇḍārho daṇḍya ityapi ||
2.d: विग्रहान्निर्वचः कार्यं समासेष्वपि तद्धिते | प्रविभज्यैव निर्भूयाद् दण्डार्हो दण्ड्य इत्यपि ||
2.e: In compounds, as well as in a secondary derivative, explanation (nirvacas) should proceed from analysis: one should explain after separating (the parts); thus 'punishable' (dand-ya) b as 'deserving punishment' (danda

2.s: bhāryā rūpavatī cāsya rūpavadbhārya ityapi | indraśca somaścetyevam indrāsāmau nidarśanam ||
2.d: भार्या रूपवती चास्य रूपवद्भार्य इत्यपि | इन्द्रश्च सोमश्चेत्येवम् इन्द्रासामौ निदर्शनम् ||

2.s: śabdarūpaṃ padārthaśca vyutpattiḥ prakṛtirguṇaḥ | sarvametadanekārthaṃ daśānavagame guṇāḥ ||
2.d: शब्दरूपं पदार्थश्च व्युत्पत्तिः प्रकृतिर्गुणः | सर्वमेतदनेकार्थं दशानवगमे गुणाः ||
2.e: The form of the sound (sabda), the sense of the word (pada), the etymology, the primary form (prakrti), the secondary element (guna), all this has manifold sense: there are ten species (gunah, scil., of explanation) in (case of) misunderstanding (anavagame).

2.s: sāmānyavācinaḥ śabdā viśeṣe sthāpitāḥ kvacit | palāyane yathā vṛttiḥ ko nu maryā itīṣate ||
2.d: सामान्यवाचिनः शब्दा विशेषे स्थापिताः क्वचित् | पलायने यथा वृत्तिः को नु मर्या इतीषते ||
2.e: Terms (sabdah) expressive of a general meaning are occasionally applied in a particular sense (visese); thus (in) 'Who, pray, O men' (ko nu maryah: viii. 45. 37), the interpretation (of) 'goes' (isate) is in (the sense of) 'fleeing'.

2.s: viśeṣavācinastvanye sāmānye sthāpitāḥ kvacit | himenāgnimiti mantre himaśabdo nidarśanam ||
2.d: विशेषवाचिनस्त्वन्ये सामान्ये स्थापिताः क्वचित् | हिमेनाग्निमिति मन्त्रे हिमशब्दो निदर्शनम् ||
2.e: But other (terms) expressive of a particular meaning are occasionally applied in a general sense; in the formula, 'With cold the fire' (himenagnim: i. 116. 8), the term 'frost'a (hima) is an example. a Yaska, in his comment on Rg-veda i. 116. 8 (Nirukta vi. 36), explains himena by udakena grismante; cp. also Sayana on i. 116. 8.

2.s: padamekaṃ samādāya dvidhā kṛtvā nirūktavān | pūruṣādaḥ padaṃ yāsko vṛkṣevṛkṣa iti tvaci ||
2.d: पदमेकं समादाय द्विधा कृत्वा निरूक्तवान् | पूरुषादः पदं यास्को वृक्षेवृक्ष इति त्वचि ||
2.e: Yaska has, in the stanza 'To every tree'a (vrkse-vrkse: x. 27. 22), explained the word 'man-eating' (purusadah) by taking one word (and) dividing (it) into two.

2.s: anekaṃ sattathā cānyad ekameva niruktavān | aruṇo mā sakṛnmantre māsakṛdvigraheṇa tu ||
2.d: अनेकं सत्तथा चान्यद् एकमेव निरुक्तवान् | अरुणो मा सकृन्मन्त्रे मासकृद्विग्रहेण तु ||
2.e: Similarly, another (expression) which is not one (word), he has explained as one only by (his) analysis as 'month-maker' (masa-krt) in the formula, 'The ruddy one me once'a (aruno ma sakrt: i. 195. 18). * In his comment on this stanza Yaska (Nirukta v. 21) explains the word as masanam karta. Our author here agrees with the Padapatha. See Roth, Erlauterungen, on Nirukta v. 21; Sayana on Rg-veda i. 195. 18; Geldner, Vedische Studien iii, p. 178.

2.s: padavyavāye'pi pade ekīkṛtya niruktavān | garbhaṃ nidhānamityete na jāmaya iti tyṛci ||
2.d: पदव्यवायेऽपि पदे एकीकृत्य निरुक्तवान् | गर्भं निधानमित्येते न जामय इति त्यृचि ||
2.e: In the stanza, 'Not to his brother' (na jamaye: iii. 31. 2), he has explained the two words garbham nidhanam, even though (another) word a intervenes, by making them into one.

2.s: padajātiravijñātā tvaḥ pade'rthaḥ śitāmani | svarānavagamo'dhāyi vane netyṛci darśitaḥ ||
2.d: पदजातिरविज्ञाता त्वः पदेऽर्थः शितामनि | स्वरानवगमोऽधायि वने नेत्यृचि दर्शितः ||
2.e: The class of word is not recognized in the word tvah, (nor) the sense in sitaman. Misunderstanding of the accent (in) adhayi is shown in the stanza As on the tree'c (vane na: x. 29. 1).

2.s: śunaḥśepaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ dyāvā naḥ pṛthivīti ca | niraskṛtetiprabhṛtiṣv arthādāsītkramo yathā ||
2.d: शुनःशेपं नराशंसं द्यावा नः पृथिवीति च | निरस्कृतेतिप्रभृतिष्व् अर्थादासीत्क्रमो यथा ||
2.e: As the regular order (of the words) was (arranged) according to the sense in Sunah-sepam, Nara-samsamc, Dyava nah prthivid, nir-askrta e, and the rest:

2.s: varṇasya varṇayorlopo bahūnāṃ vyañjanasya ca | atrāṇīti kapirnābhā dano yāmītyaghāsu ca ||
2.d: वर्णस्य वर्णयोर्लोपो बहूनां व्यञ्जनस्य च | अत्राणीति कपिर्नाभा दनो यामीत्यघासु च ||
2.e: (so) there is dropping of a letter (varna), of two letters, of many, and of a consonant: (for instance, in) atrani, kapih, nabhac, danahd, yamie, and aghasu f.

2.s: arthātpadaṃ svābhidheyaṃ padādvākyārthanirṇayaḥ | padasaṃghātajaṃ vākyaṃ varṇasaṃghātajaṃ padam ||
2.d: अर्थात्पदं स्वाभिधेयं पदाद्वाक्यार्थनिर्णयः | पदसंघातजं वाक्यं वर्णसंघातजं पदम् ||
2.e: From the sense (comes) the word (pada), its designation; from the word (comes) the ascertainment of the sense of the sentence (vakya). (For) the sentence arises from an aggregation of words, the word arises from an aggregation of letters.

2.s: arthātprakaraṇālliṅgād aucityāddeśakālataḥ | mantreṣvarthavivekaḥ syād itareṣviti ca sthitiḥ ||
2.d: अर्थात्प्रकरणाल्लिङ्गाद् औचित्याद्देशकालतः | मन्त्रेष्वर्थविवेकः स्याद् इतरेष्विति च स्थितिः ||
2.e: From the sense (of the word), the subject-matter (prakarana), the gender, the appropriateness, and from (considerations of) place and time, the (possibility of) discriminating the (whole) sense in the formulas will result; such is the settled rule (sthitih) in (regard to) other (writings) also. There is a lacuna in b from 118 ed to 122 ed mantravi ]ttamaih |

2.s: iti nānānvayopāyair nairukte yo yateta saḥ | jijñāsurbrahmaṇo rūpam api duṣkṛtparaṃ vrajet ||
2.d: इति नानान्वयोपायैर् नैरुक्ते यो यतेत सः | जिज्ञासुर्ब्रह्मणो रूपम् अपि दुष्कृत्परं व्रजेत् ||
2.e: He who thus exerts himself in the study of etymology (nairukte) by the various means of construing (anvaya), being desirous of knowing the form of Brahma, will, even though an evil-doer, go to the supreme (param).

2.s: yathedamagre naivāsīd asadapyathavāpi sat | jajñe yathedaṃ sarvaṃ tad bhāvavṛttaṃ vadanti tu ||
2.d: यथेदमग्रे नैवासीद् असदप्यथवापि सत् | जज्ञे यथेदं सर्वं तद् भाववृत्तं वदन्ति तु ||
2.e: How this (world) did not exist in the beginning, either as non-existent or existent, how this universe (sarvam) came into being, (all) this they term the evolution (vrttam) of becoming (bhava). yathedamagre hdm',yathedamame, yayedamagne [k.

2.s: bhāvapradhānamākhyātaṃ ṣaḍvikārā bhavanti te | janmāstitvaṃ parīṇāmo vṛddhirhānaṃ vināśanam ||
2.d: भावप्रधानमाख्यातं षड्विकारा भवन्ति ते | जन्मास्तित्वं परीणामो वृद्धिर्हानं विनाशनम् ||
2.e: The verb (akhyata) has becoming as its fundamental meaning (pradhana). There are these six modifications (vikarah) b of becoming: genesis (janma), existence (astitvam), transformation (parinamah), growth (vrddhih), decline (hanam), destruction (vinasanam).

2.s: eteṣāmeva ṣaṇṇāṃ tu ye'nye bhāvavikārajāḥ | te yathāvākyamabhyūhyāḥ sāmarthyānmantravittamaiḥ ||
2.d: एतेषामेव षण्णां तु येऽन्ये भावविकारजाः | ते यथावाक्यमभ्यूह्याः सामर्थ्यान्मन्त्रवित्तमैः ||
2.e: But whatever other modifications of becoming arise from these six a must be inferred in each case according to the sentence, to the best of their ability (samarthyat), by those who are most familiar with the formulas, II.

2.s: devānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca namaskāraistathaiva ca | atha vyastaṃ samastaṃ vā śṛṇu vyāhṛtidaivatam ||
2.d: देवानां च पितॄणां च नमस्कारैस्तथैव च | अथ व्यस्तं समस्तं वा शृणु व्याहृतिदैवतम् ||

2.s: vyāhṛtīnāṃ samastānāṃ daivataṃ tu prajāpatiḥ | vyastānāmayamagniśca vāyuḥ sūryaśca devatāḥ ||
2.d: व्याहृतीनां समस्तानां दैवतं तु प्रजापतिः | व्यस्तानामयमग्निश्च वायुः सूर्यश्च देवताः ||
2.e: Now the divinity of the sacred utterances collectively is Prajapati (a), while the deities of them individually are this (terrestrial) Agni, Vayu, and Surya (respectively).

2.s: vāgdevatyo'thavāpyaindro yadi vā parameṣṭhinaḥ | oṃkāro vaiśvadevo vā brāhmo daivaḥ ka eva vā ||
2.d: वाग्देवत्योऽथवाप्यैन्द्रो यदि वा परमेष्ठिनः | ओंकारो वैश्वदेवो वा ब्राह्मो दैवः क एव वा ||
2.e: The syllable Om has Vac for its deity, or else it is addressed to Indra, or else (it belongs) to Paramesthin; or it is addressed to the All-gods, or to Brahman, or to the Gods (in general), or Ka (is its deity).

2.s: āgneyaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ madhuchandasa ārṣakam | jñeyāḥ sarve'nyadevatyās tṛcāḥ saptāta uttarāḥ ||
2.d: आग्नेयं प्रथमं सूक्तं मधुछन्दस आर्षकम् | ज्ञेयाः सर्वेऽन्यदेवत्यास् तृचाः सप्तात उत्तराः ||
2.e: The first hymn is addressed to Agni. Its seer a is Madhuchandas. The seven triplets b which follow it should all be recognized as addressed to different deities.

2.s: vāyavyaḥ prathamastveṣām endravāyava uttaraḥ | maitrāvaruṇo'thāśvino'pyaindro'to vaiśvadevakaḥ ||
2.d: वायव्यः प्रथमस्त्वेषाम् एन्द्रवायव उत्तरः | मैत्रावरुणोऽथाश्विनोऽप्यैन्द्रोऽतो वैश्वदेवकः ||
2.e: The first of these (2. 1-3) is addressed to Vayu, the following one (2. 4-6) to Indra and Vayu, then one to Mitra and Varuna (2. 7-9), one also to the Asvins (3. 1-3), one to Indra (3. 4-6), then one to the All-gods (3. 7-9).

2.s: tannāmā viśvaliṅgo vā gāyatro'ntyastu yastṛcaḥ | bahudaivatamanyattu vaiśvadeveṣu śasyate ||
2.d: तन्नामा विश्वलिङ्गो वा गायत्रोऽन्त्यस्तु यस्तृचः | बहुदैवतमन्यत्तु वैश्वदेवेषु शस्यते ||
2.e: Now (this) last triplet (3. 7-9), composed in the Gayatri metre, contains that name (tan-nama), or has (the word) 'all' (visva) as its characteristic mark. But (any) other (hymn) addressed to many divinities can be recited in (the place of) those addressed to the All-gods.

2.s: luśe duvasyau śāryāte gotame'tha ṛjiśvani | avatsāre parucchepe atrau dīrghatamasyṛṣau ||
2.d: लुशे दुवस्यौ शार्याते गोतमेऽथ ऋजिश्वनि | अवत्सारे परुच्छेपे अत्रौ दीर्घतमस्यृषौ ||
2.e: In Lusa, Duvasyu, Saryatad, Gotama, Rjisvan f, Avatsara, Paruchepa h, Atrii, the seer Dirghatamas j, duvasyau x, tha

2.s: vasiṣṭhe nābhānediṣṭhe gaye medhātithau manau | kakṣīvati vihavye ca bahuṣvanyeṣvatharṣiṣu ||
2.d: वसिष्ठे नाभानेदिष्ठे गये मेधातिथौ मनौ | कक्षीवति विहव्ये च बहुष्वन्येष्वथर्षिषु ||

2.s: agastye bṛhadukthe ca viśvāmitre ca gāthini | dṛśyante vipravādāśca tāsu tāsu stutiṣviha ||
2.d: अगस्त्ये बृहदुक्थे च विश्वामित्रे च गाथिनि | दृश्यन्ते विप्रवादाश्च तासु तासु स्तुतिष्विह ||

2.s: bahvīnāṃ saṃnipātastu yasminmantre pradṛśyate | ācāryau yāskaśāṇḍilyau vaiśvadevaṃ tadāhatuḥ ||
2.d: बह्वीनां संनिपातस्तु यस्मिन्मन्त्रे प्रदृश्यते | आचार्यौ यास्कशाण्डिल्यौ वैश्वदेवं तदाहतुः ||
2.e: Now the teachers Yaska a and Sandilya say that any formula b in which a combination of many (deities) appears, is addressed to the All-gods.

2.s: pādaṃ vā yadi vārdharcam ṛcaṃ vā sūktameva vā | vaiśvadevaṃ vadetsarvaṃ yatkiṃcidbahudaivatam ||
2.d: पादं वा यदि वार्धर्चम् ऋचं वा सूक्तमेव वा | वैश्वदेवं वदेत्सर्वं यत्किंचिद्बहुदैवतम् ||
2.e: One should state everything, whatever it be, a verse, or hemistich, or stanza, or hymn, which is addressed to many divinities, to be addressed to the All-gods.

2.s: ṛṣibhirdevatāḥ sarvā viśvābhi stutibhi stutāḥ | saṃjñā tu viśvamityeṣā sarvāvāptau nipātitā ||
2.d: ऋषिभिर्देवताः सर्वा विश्वाभि स्तुतिभि स्तुताः | संज्ञा तु विश्वमित्येषा सर्वावाप्तौ निपातिता ||
2.e: All (sarvah) the deities are praised by the seers with collective laudations; now this technical term (samjna) 'collective' (visva) is laid down (nipatita) in (the sense of) all-comprehensivenessa (sarvavaptau). - 3. The words sarva to stutah (inclusive) are

2.s: sārasvatastu saptama etāḥ praugadevatāḥ | sarasvatīti dvividham ṛkṣu sarvāsu sā stutā ||
2.d: सारस्वतस्तु सप्तम एताः प्रौगदेवताः | सरस्वतीति द्विविधम् ऋक्षु सर्वासु सा स्तुता ||
2.e: Now the seventh (triplet) is addressed to Sarasvati (3. 10-12). These are the Prauga deities. She is praised in all stanzas by the name of Sarasvati in two ways:

2.s: nadāvaddevatāvaśca tatrācāryastu śaunakaḥ | nadīvannigamāḥ ṣaṭ te saptamo netyuvāca ha ||
2.d: नदावद्देवतावश्च तत्राचार्यस्तु शौनकः | नदीवन्निगमाः षट् ते सप्तमो नेत्युवाच ह ||

2.s: ambyekā ca dṛṣadvatyāṃ citra icca sarasvatī | iyaṃ śuṣmebhirityetaṃ mene yāskastu saptamam ||
2.d: अम्ब्येका च दृषद्वत्यां चित्र इच्च सरस्वती | इयं शुष्मेभिरित्येतं मेने यास्कस्तु सप्तमम् ||
2.e: (the six being) 'Best Mother' (ambi-tame: ii. 41. 6), 'Alone' (eka vii. 95. 2), 'On the Drsadvati' (drsadvatyam: iii. 23. 4), Citra indeed' (citra it: viii. 21. 18), 'Sarasvati' (x. 64. 9 and vi. 52. 6). Yaska, however, regarded this (passage), 'She with her might' (iyam susmebhih: vi. 61. 2), to be a seventh.

2.s: paśoḥ sārasvatasyaitāṃ yājyāṃ maitrāyaṇīyake | prādhānyāddhaviṣaḥ paśyan vāca evaitaro'bravīt ||
2.d: पशोः सारस्वतस्यैतां याज्यां मैत्रायणीयके | प्राधान्याद्धविषः पश्यन् वाच एवैतरोऽब्रवीत् ||
2.e: Aitara a regarding this (stanza) as a sacrificial text (yajya) for the victim offered to Sarasvati (sarasvata) in the Maitrayaniya (Samhita), because the oblation is (here) the chief thing, has stated (that it is addressed) to Vac. i

2.s: surūpakṛtnumityaindraṃ sapta cānyānyataḥ param | ṣaḻādaha svadhāmanu mārutyo'nantarā ṛcaḥ ||
2.d: सुरूपकृत्नुमित्यैन्द्रं सप्त चान्यान्यतः परम् | षḻआदह स्वधामनु मारुत्योऽनन्तरा ऋचः ||
2.e: (The hymn) 'Doer of fair deeds' (surupakrtnum: i. 4) is addressed to Indra, as well as seven others after it (5-11). Six successive stanzas (beginning) Then according to their wont' (ad aha svadham anu: 6. 4-9) are addressed to the Maruts.

2.s: ekā vīḻu cidindrāya marudbhiḥ saha gīyate | tasyā ekāntarāyāstu ardharco'ntyo dvidevataḥ ||
2.d: एका वीḻउ चिदिन्द्राय मरुद्भिः सह गीयते | तस्या एकान्तरायास्तु अर्धर्चोऽन्त्यो द्विदेवतः ||
2.e: One (of them), 'What is firm' (vilu cit: 6. 5) is sung in honour of Indra with the Maruts. But the latter hemistich of the (stanza) next but one to this (i. e. 6. 7) a is addressed to two deities.

2.s: marudgaṇapradhāno hītthaṃ cendro vicikitsitaḥ | mandū samānavarcasā mandunā vā savarcasā ||
2.d: मरुद्गणप्रधानो हीत्थं चेन्द्रो विचिकित्सितः | मन्दू समानवर्चसा मन्दुना वा सवर्चसा ||
2.e: For while it is chiefly addressed to the host of the Maruts, Indra is at the same time intended to be distinguished thus: 'both glad (and) equal in brilliance' (mandu samanavarcasa); or (this means) with him who is glad (and) of equal brilliance'.

2.s: mandū iti pragṛhṇanti yeṣāmeva dvidevataḥ | ekadevatyamāśrāvyo vijñāyādhyayanātpadam ||
2.d: मन्दू इति प्रगृह्णन्ति येषामेव द्विदेवतः | एकदेवत्यमाश्राव्यो विज्ञायाध्ययनात्पदम् ||
2.e: Those to whom (the hemistich appears to be) addressed to two deities, explain (the final vowel of) mandu as not liable to phonetic combination (pragrhnanti). One (however) who from his study (of it) recognizes the pada to have only one deity, deserves a hearing;

2.s: rodasī devapatnīnām atharvāṅgirase yathā | marudgaṇapradhāneyam ācāryāṇāṃ stutirmatā ||
2.d: रोदसी देवपत्नीनाम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसे यथा | मरुद्गणप्रधानेयम् आचार्याणां स्तुतिर्मता ||

2.s: marudgaṇapradhānatvād indrastu vicikitsitaḥ | marudgaṇaṃ mahendrasya samāṃśaṃ sakalaṃ viduḥ ||
2.d: मरुद्गणप्रधानत्वाद् इन्द्रस्तु विचिकित्सितः | मरुद्गणं महेन्द्रस्य समांशं सकलं विदुः ||
2.e: As the host of the Maruts is chiefly addressed, Indra is at the same time intended to be distinguished. For the entire host of the Maruts is considered to share (in sacrifice) equally (samamsam) with the great Indra.

2.s: agnimityagnidaivatyaṃ pādastatra dvidevataḥ | nirmathyāhavanīyārthāv agnināgniḥ samidhyate ||
2.d: अग्निमित्यग्निदैवत्यं पादस्तत्र द्विदेवतः | निर्मथ्याहवनीयार्थाव् अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते ||
2.e: The hymn 'Agni' (agnim: i. 12) has Agni as its divinity. In it one verse, 'by Agni Agni is kindled'

2.s: 'pādo dvadhagnidaivato nirmathyāhavanīyau' | dvitīye dvādaśarce tu pratyṛcaṃ yāstu devatāḥ | stūyante hyagninā sārdhaṃ tāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu ||
2.d: ऽपादो द्वधग्निदैवतो निर्मथ्याहवनीयौ' | द्वितीये द्वादशर्चे तु प्रत्यृचं यास्तु देवताः | स्तूयन्ते ह्यग्निना सार्धं तासां नामानि मे शृणु ||
2.e: Now as to the deities which, stanza by stanza, in the second hymn of twelve stanzas (i. 13), are praised along with Agni, hear their names from me.

2.s: prathamāyāṃ stutaścedhmo dvitīyāyāṃ tanūnapāt | narāśaṃsastṛtīyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ stūyate tviḻaḥ ||
2.d: प्रथमायां स्तुतश्चेध्मो द्वितीयायां तनूनपात् | नराशंसस्तृतीयायां चतुर्थ्यां स्तूयते त्विḻअः ||
2.e: In the first (stanza) Fuel (idhma) is praised, in the second Tanunapat, Narasamsa in the third, but in the fourth Ila is

2.s: barhireva tu pañcamyāṃ dvāro devyastato'nyayā | naktoṣāsā tu saptamyām aṣṭamyāṃ saṃstutau saha ||
2.d: बर्हिरेव तु पञ्चम्यां द्वारो देव्यस्ततोऽन्यया | नक्तोषासा तु सप्तम्याम् अष्टम्यां संस्तुतौ सह ||

2.s: daivyāviti tu hotārau navamyāmṛci saṃstutāḥ | tisro devyo daśamyāṃ tu jñeyastvaṣṭaiva tu stutaḥ ||
2.d: दैव्याविति तु होतारौ नवम्यामृचि संस्तुताः | तिस्रो देव्यो दशम्यां तु ज्ञेयस्त्वष्टैव तु स्तुतः ||

2.s: ekādaśyāṃ tu sūktasya stutaṃ vidyādvanaspatim | dvādaśyāṃ tu stutā devīr vidyātsvāhākṛtīriti ||
2.d: एकादश्यां तु सूक्तस्य स्तुतं विद्याद्वनस्पतिम् | द्वादश्यां तु स्तुता देवीर् विद्यात्स्वाहाकृतीरिति ||
2.e: In the eleventh (stanza) of the hymn one should know Vanaspati to be praised, but in the twelfth one should know the divine 'Svahakrtis' to be praised.

2.s: sūkte'sminpratyṛcaṃ yāstu devatā parikīrtitāḥ | tā eva sarvāsvāprīṣu dvitīyā tu vikalpate ||
2.d: सूक्तेऽस्मिन्प्रत्यृचं यास्तु देवता परिकीर्तिताः | ता एव सर्वास्वाप्रीषु द्वितीया तु विकल्पते ||
2.e: Now as to the deities which, stanza by stanza, are celebrated in this hymn (i. 13), they (occur) in all the Apris; the second (deity), however, is subject to option (vikalpate). °ya tu

2.s: praiṣaiḥ sahāprīsūktāni tānyekādaśa santi ca | yajūṃṣi praiṣasūktaṃ vā daśaitānītarāṇi tu ||
2.d: प्रैषैः सहाप्रीसूक्तानि तान्येकादश सन्ति च | यजूंषि प्रैषसूक्तं वा दशैतानीतराणि तु ||
2.e: As to the Apri hymns, including the Praisas (ritual summons), they are eleven (in number); or (rather) the Praisa hymn (consists of) sacrificial formulas, while these other (hymns of the Rg-veda) are ten (in number).

2.s: sautrāmaṇāni tu trīṇi prājāpatyāśvamedhike | puruṣasya tu yanmedhe yajuḥṣveva tu tāni ṣaṭ ||
2.d: सौत्रामणानि तु त्रीणि प्राजापत्याश्वमेधिके | पुरुषस्य तु यन्मेधे यजुःष्वेव तु तानि षट् ||
2.e: Now there are three (Apri hymns) relating to the Sautramani sacrifice (sautramanani), one to Prajapati (prajapatya), and one used at the horse-sacrifice (asvamedhika), and the one (employed) in the human sacrifice (purusasya medhe): these (make) six (special additional Apri hymns) in the Yajur-veda (yajuhsu).

2.s: atraiva praiṣasūktaṃ syān na yajuḥṣvādriyeta tat | teṣāṃ praiṣagataṃ sūktaṃ yacca dīrghatamā jagau ||
2.d: अत्रैव प्रैषसूक्तं स्यान् न यजुःष्वाद्रियेत तत् | तेषां प्रैषगतं सूक्तं यच्च दीर्घतमा जगौ ||
2.e: Here only the Praisa hymn (Vajasaneyi Samhita xxi. 29-40) need be (considered); that (which has been referred to beyond this) in the Yajur-veda (yajuhsu) need not be troubled about (here). Of those (eleven) the hymn relating to the Praisas, and that which Dirghatamas sang (i.

2.s: medhātithau yaduktaṃ ca trīṇyevobhayavanti tu | ṛṣau gṛtsamade yacca vādhryaśve ca yaducyate ||
2.d: मेधातिथौ यदुक्तं च त्रीण्येवोभयवन्ति तु | ऋषौ गृत्समदे यच्च वाध्र्यश्वे च यदुच्यते ||

2.s: narāśaṃsavadatreśca dadarśa ca yadaurvaśaḥ | tanūnapādagastyaśca jamadagniśca yajjagau ||
2.d: नराशंसवदत्रेश्च ददर्श च यदौर्वशः | तनूनपादगस्त्यश्च जमदग्निश्च यज्जगौ ||

2.s: viśvāmitra ṛṣiryaśca jagau vai kāśyapo'sitaḥ | medhātitherṛcāṃ yāstu proktā dvādaśa devatāḥ ||
2.d: विश्वामित्र ऋषिर्यश्च जगौ वै काश्यपोऽसितः | मेधातिथेरृचां यास्तु प्रोक्ता द्वादश देवताः ||

2.s: saṃpadyante yathāgniṃ tāḥ saṃpadaṃ tāṃ nibodhata | idhmo yaḥ sarvamevāgnir ayaṃ hīdhmaḥ samidhyate ||
2.d: संपद्यन्ते यथाग्निं ताः संपदं तां निबोधत | इध्मो यः सर्वमेवाग्निर् अयं हीध्मः समिध्यते ||

2.s: dhmātervai tatkṛtaṃ rūpaṃ dhmāto hīdhmaḥ samidhyate ||
2.d: ध्मातेर्वै तत्कृतं रूपं ध्मातो हीध्मः समिध्यते ||

3.s: tanūnapādayaṃ tveva nāmnā yacchatyasau tanum | nāpāditi prajāmāhur amuto'sya ca saṃbhavam ||
3.d: तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्छत्यसौ तनुम् | नापादिति प्रजामाहुर् अमुतोऽस्य च संभवम् ||

3.s: narāśaṃsamihaike tu agnimāhurathetare | narāḥ śaṃsanti sarve'sminn āsīnā iti vādhvare ||
3.d: नराशंसमिहैके तु अग्निमाहुरथेतरे | नराः शंसन्ति सर्वेऽस्मिन्न् आसीना इति वाध्वरे ||
3.e: Now some say that Narasamsa here is Agnia. Again (atha va) others (use the term) in (the sense of) sacrifice, (saying) 'all men (narah) utter praise (samsanti) seated at it.'

3.s: etamevāhuranye'gniṃ narāśaṃso'dhvare hyayam | naraiḥ praśasya āsīnair āhuścairṛtvijo naraḥ ||
3.d: एतमेवाहुरन्येऽग्निं नराशंसोऽध्वरे ह्ययम् | नरैः प्रशस्य आसीनैर् आहुश्चैरृत्विजो नरः ||
3.e: Others say he is Agni, because he is Narasamsa as the object of praise (prasasya) by men seated at the sacrifice; and so also say the ritualists (rtvijo narah).

3.s: iḻastvṛṣikṛtaṃ rūpama īḍeśca stutikarmaṇaḥ | iḻāvāṃstena vokto'gnir iḍinā varddhikarmaṇā ||
3.d: इḻअस्त्वृषिकृतं रूपम ईडेश्च स्तुतिकर्मणः | इḻआवांस्तेन वोक्तोऽग्निर् इडिना वर्द्धिकर्मणा ||
3.e: Ila is a form made by the Rishis, and (is derived) from the root id, expressing praise: Agni is called ilavan (* possessing 78 refreshment ') either from that (root) or from the root id, expressing increase. r.

3.s: barhirevāyamagnistu sarvaṃ hi paribṛṃhitam | annena yaddhato vā sann idhmena paribṛṃhitaḥ ||
3.d: बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिबृंहितम् | अन्नेन यद्धतो वा सन्न् इध्मेन परिबृंहितः ||
3.e: Again, this Agni is the Litter (barhis), for the whole of it (sarvam) is furnished (paribrmhitam) with food, or because, when sacrificed to, he (Agni ) is furnished ( paribymhitah) b with fuel.

3.s: dvārastu devyau yāḥ proktā viśveṣāṃ tāstu patnayaḥ | agnāyīmanuvartante tathāgnāyyagnimeva ca ||
3.d: द्वारस्तु देव्यौ याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां तास्तु पत्नयः | अग्नायीमनुवर्तन्ते तथाग्नाय्यग्निमेव च ||
3.e: The Divine Doors, as they are called, are the wives of all (the gods) * ; they follow Agnayi, and so also Agnayi (follows) Agni. i. 13. 7 arcy r, arce, ahm1r3fkr2r3r 7 (on this corruption cp. critical note on i. 92). The MSS. have the correct form in i. 107 and ii. 148.

3.s: .agnau dhruvaṃ sthitāstāstu saṃstūyante'gninā saha | prādhānyaṃ tāsu kaivāgne stutiṣveva haviḥṣu ca ||
3.d: .अग्नौ ध्रुवं स्थितास्तास्तु संस्तूयन्तेऽग्निना सह | प्राधान्यं तासु कैवाग्ने स्तुतिष्वेव हविःषु च ||
3.e: Now being firmly established in Agni they are praised in combination with Agni. In their case also there is a predominance of Agni, both in praises and oblations.

3.s: naktoṣāsau ca ye devyāv āgneyyāveva te smṛte | śyāvyāgneyī hi kālasya tasyaivoṣāḥ kaleva tu ||
3.d: नक्तोषासौ च ये देव्याव् आग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते | श्याव्याग्नेयी हि कालस्य तस्यैवोषाः कलेव तु ||
3.e: And as to the two goddesses, Night and Dawn (naktosasau), they too are regarded as related to Agni. For the Dark (syavi) is related to Agni, while Dawn is, as it were, a sixteenth portion (kala) of that time (kala).

3.s: tama ucchatyuṣā naktānaktīmāṃ himabindubhiḥ | api vāvyaktavarṇeti nañpūrvāñceridaṃ bhavet ||
3.d: तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तीमां हिमबिन्दुभिः | अपि वाव्यक्तवर्णेति नञ्पूर्वाञ्चेरिदं भवेत् ||
3.e: Dawn (usas) lightens (uchati) the darkness, Night (nakta) anoints (anakti) b her with drops of dew (hima); or else this (form) might be (derived) from the root anc, preceded by the negative (nan) e, (and) mean 'the indefinite-coloured one' (avyaktavarna) f.

3.s: sā hi doṣā bhavatyādau niśīthe sā tamasvatī | nāmnā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāgudayādraveḥ ||
3.d: सा हि दोषा भवत्यादौ निशीथे सा तमस्वती | नाम्ना भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ||
3.e: For at first she becomes Gloaming (dosa), at midnight she is Darkling (tamasvati), and before the rising of the Sun she becomes Dawn (usas) by name. dosa

3.s: devyāviti tu hotārāv agni pārthivamadhyamau | divyādagnerhi jajñāte daivyau teneha janmanā ||
3.d: देव्याविति तु होताराव् अग्नि पार्थिवमध्यमौ | दिव्यादग्नेर्हि जज्ञाते दैव्यौ तेनेह जन्मना ||
3.e: Now the Two Divine Sacrificers are the terrestrial and the middle (forms of) Agnia. For they were born from the celestial (divya) Agni; they are therefore celestial (daivya) b by birth.

3.s: tisrastu devyo yāḥ proktās tristhānaiveha sā tu vāk | trividhenocyate nāmnā jyotiḥṣu triṣu vartinī ||
3.d: तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास् त्रिस्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् | त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्ना ज्योतिःषु त्रिषु वर्तिनी ||
3.e: Now they who are called the Three Goddesses are here simply (representative of) Speech (Vac) in the three spheres. She is spoken of by a threefold name a as abiding in the three lights.

3.s: agnimevānugeḻā tu madhyaṃ prāptā sarasvatī | amuṃ sthitādhi lokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau ||
3.d: अग्निमेवानुगेḻआ तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती | अमुं स्थिताधि लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ||
3.e: Ila follows (the terrestrial) Agni, Sarasvati b is attached to (prapta), the middle one, while that (celestial form of Vac) becomes Bharati as occupying that (celestial) world.

3.s: saiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi ca vyomni ceha ca | vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajatyagnīnimānapi ||
3.d: सैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्नि चेह च | व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीनिमानपि ||
3.e: Now this same Vac is threefold (as) in heaven and in air and here (on earth). Both when individual and combined she belongs (bhajati) to a all these (three) Agnis.

3.s: tvaṣṭā tu yastvayameva pārthivo'gniriti stutiḥ | pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syuḥ kasyāpyṛk cārtaveṣu ca ||
3.d: त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः | पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्युः कस्याप्यृक् चार्तवेषु च ||
3.e: Now as to Tvastr, there is praise (of him) as this same terrestrial Agni; or (it may be said) there are stanzas b to him as terrestrial, and there is one stanza also in the (hymns) to the seasons (addressed) to (him as) one or other (kasyapi, form of Agni).

3.s: tviṣitastvakṣatervā syāt tṛrṇamaśnuta eva vā | karsmasṛ'ttāraṇo veti tena nāmaitadaśnute ||
3.d: त्विषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् तृर्णमश्नुत एव वा | कर्स्मसृऽत्तारणो वेति तेन नामैतदश्नुते ||
3.e: (Tvastr) may be (derived) from tvis or from tvaks, or (it means) he quickly (turnam) obtains (asnute)'a, or 'he assists (ut-tarana) in works (karmasu)'b; therefore he obtains this name.

3.s: yaḥ sahasratamo raśmī raveścandramupāśritaḥ | so'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ ceha ca yanmadhu ||
3.d: यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्चन्द्रमुपाश्रितः | सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मधु ||
3.e: The thousandfold ray of the sun which abides in the moon, as well as the mead (madhu) which is above (param) and on earth (iha), also (abides) in the Tvastr (who is) Agni.

3.s: prādādbrahmāpi suprītaḥ sutāya tadatharvaṇaḥ | sa cābhavadṛṣistena brahmaṇā dīptimattaraḥ ||
3.d: प्रादाद्ब्रह्मापि सुप्रीतः सुताय तदथर्वणः | स चाभवदृषिस्तेन ब्रह्मणा दीप्तिमत्तरः ||

3.s: tamṛṣiṃ niṣiṣedhendro maivaṃ vocaḥ kvacinmadhu | na hi prākte madhunyasmiñ jīvantaṃtvotsṛjāmyaham ||
3.d: तमृषिं निषिषेधेन्द्रो मैवं वोचः क्वचिन्मधु | न हि प्राक्ते मधुन्यस्मिञ् जीवन्तंत्वोत्सृजाम्यहम् ||
3.e: Indra forbade the sage (saying), 'Do not speak anywhere of the mead thus (revealed); for if this mead is proclaimed (to any one), I will not let you escape alive.'

3.s: tamṛṣiṃ tvaśvinau devau vivakte madhvayācatām | sa ca tābhyāṃ tadācaṣṭe yaduvāca śacīpatiḥ ||
3.d: तमृषिं त्वश्विनौ देवौ विवक्ते मध्वयाचताम् | स च ताभ्यां तदाचष्टे यदुवाच शचीपतिः ||
3.e: Now the divine Asvins asked for the mead in secret from the seer; and he told them what the Lord of Saci had said.

3.s: tamabrūtāṃ tu nāsatyāv āśvyena śirasā bhavān | madhvāśu grāhayatvāvāṃ mendraśca tvā vadhīttataḥ ||
3.d: तमब्रूतां तु नासत्याव् आश्व्येन शिरसा भवान् | मध्वाशु ग्राहयत्वावां मेन्द्रश्च त्वा वधीत्ततः ||
3.e: To him the Nasatyas spake: 'Do you quickly make us two receive the mead by means of a horse's head; Indra shall not slay you for that.'

3.s: āśvyena śirasā tau tu dadhyaṅṅāha yadaśvinau | tadasyendro'haratsvaṃ tan nyadhattāmasya yacchiraḥ ||
3.d: आश्व्येन शिरसा तौ तु दध्यङ्ङाह यदश्विनौ | तदस्येन्द्रोऽहरत्स्वं तन् न्यधत्तामस्य यच्छिरः ||
3.e: Because Dadhyanc had told (the secret) to the two Asvins with the horse's head, Indra took off that (head) of his ; ( but) his own head they (the Asvins) put on (again).

3.s: dadhīcaśca śiraścāśvyaṃ kṛtaṃ vajreṇa vajriṇā | papāta saraso madhye parvate śaryaṇāvato ||
3.d: दधीचश्च शिरश्चाश्व्यं कृतं वज्रेण वज्रिणा | पपात सरसो मध्ये पर्वते शर्यणावतो ||
3.e: And the horse's head of Dadhyanc, severed by the boltbearer with his bolt, fell in the midst of a lake on Mount Saryanavat.

3.s: tadadbhyastu samutthāya bhūtebhyo vividhānvarān | prādāya yugaparyantaṃ yāsvevāpsu nimajjati ||
3.d: तदद्भ्यस्तु समुत्थाय भूतेभ्यो विविधान्वरान् | प्रादाय युगपर्यन्तं यास्वेवाप्सु निमज्जति ||
3.e: Rising up from the waters (and) bestowing manifold boons on living beings, it lies submerged in those same waters to the close of the cosmic age (yuga).

3.s: tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo'sau mādhyamike gaṇe | stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ tasya na vidyate ||
3.d: त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे | स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं तस्य न विद्यते ||
3.e: That Tvastr, who is in the group of the middle sphere (madhyamika), is a modifier (vikartr) b of forms. He too is praised incidentally; a hymn to him does not exist.

3.s: vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhur ayaṃ so'gnirvanaspatiḥ | ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayatīti vā ||
3.d: वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुर् अयं सोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः | अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयतीति वा ||
3.e: Now he whom they proclaim as Vanaspati is this (ayam) Agni a as Lord of the Wood; for this (Agni) is lord (pati) of woods as (their) protector (pata), or because he guards (palayati) them.

3.s: agnirgṛtsamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīḻitaḥ | mandasvetyasya sūktasya ṣaḻṛcasya tṛtīyayā ||
3.d: अग्निर्गृत्समदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीḻइतः | मन्दस्वेत्यस्य सूक्तस्य षḻऋचस्य तृतीयया ||
3.e: This (ayam) Agni is also lauded as Vanaspati by Grtsamada in the third (stanza) a of the hymn 'Enjoy' (mandasva: ii. 37), which contains six stanzas.

3.s: yūpavattaruvaccaiva stutiryāsya prasaṅgajā | sarveṇāñjanti sūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṇḍale ||
3.d: यूपवत्तरुवच्चैव स्तुतिर्यास्य प्रसङ्गजा | सर्वेणाञ्जन्ति सूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मण्डले ||
3.e: But an occasional (prasangaja) praise of him (Vanaspati), as a sacrificial post a and as a tree, with the whole b hymn, 'They anoint' (anjanti: iii. 8), is (to be found) in the third Mandala.

3.s: svāhākṛtayo'nekāśca viduṣāṃ matayo'bhavan | tatsarvaṃ tvayamevāgnir bhavatīti viniścayaḥ ||
3.d: स्वाहाकृतयोऽनेकाश्च विदुषां मतयोऽभवन् | तत्सर्वं त्वयमेवाग्निर् भवतीति विनिश्चयः ||
3.e: As to the Svahakrtis-the views of the learned have been various. It is, however, a certain conclusion that all that (viz. which is meant by the term) a is simply (a form of) this Agni.

3.s: ayaṃ hi kartā svāhānāṃ kṛtistāsāmihaikajā | ayaṃ prasūtirbhūtānāṃ sarveṣāmayamavyayaḥ ||
3.d: अयं हि कर्ता स्वाहानां कृतिस्तासामिहैकजा | अयं प्रसूतिर्भूतानां सर्वेषामयमव्ययः ||
3.e: For he is the maker (karta) of oblations (svaha); the making (krti) of them, (that is to say,) here is of a single nature (ekaja) a it is he who is the source (prasuti) of living beings, the imperishable (source) of all of them. hi

3.s: tanūnapāddvitāyā ca narāśaṃsavatī ca yā | samasyete prayoktavye triṣvevobhayavatsu tu ||
3.d: तनूनपाद्द्विताया च नराशंसवती च या | समस्येते प्रयोक्तव्ये त्रिष्वेवोभयवत्सु तु ||
3.e: Both the second (stanza) with Tanunapat and that which contains Narasamsa, are combined as applicable (prayoktavye) in only three (hymns) which (thus) contain both.

3.s: narāśaṃsavatī vā syād dvitīyā ca prajārthinām | balakāmo'nnakāmo vā bhūtimicchedathāpi yaḥ ||
3.d: नराशंसवती वा स्याद् द्वितीया च प्रजार्थिनाम् | बलकामोऽन्नकामो वा भूतिमिच्छेदथापि यः ||
3.e: The (stanza) containing Narasamsa, as well as the second, may be (applied in behalf) b of those wanting children, (of him) who desires strength or who desires food, as well as (of him) who may wish for prosperity.

3.s: āgneyaṃ sūktamaibhiryad vaiśvadevamihocyate | tadviśvaliṅgaṃ gāyatraṃ vaiśvadeveṣu śasyate ||
3.d: आग्नेयं सूक्तमैभिर्यद् वैश्वदेवमिहोच्यते | तद्विश्वलिङ्गं गायत्रं वैश्वदेवेषु शस्यते ||
3.e: The hymn, 'Hither with these' (aibhih: i. 14), which invoking Agni a is spoken of here as addressed to the All-gods (vaisvadeva), is recited (sasyate) among the hymns to the Allgods, because, being composed in the gayatri metre, it contains the characteristic All' (visva).

3.s: indra somaṃ pibetīdaṃ yaddvādaśakamārtavam | tasminsahartunā sapta pratyṛcaṃ stauti devatāḥ ||
3.d: इन्द्र सोमं पिबेतीदं यद्द्वादशकमार्तवम् | तस्मिन्सहर्तुना सप्त प्रत्यृचं स्तौति देवताः ||
3.e: As to the hymn, 'Indra, drink Soma' (i. 15), consisting of twelve stanzas, and addressed to the Seasons, (the seer) praises in it seven deities b in their respective stanzas, together with the Season (rtu).

3.s: tatrartuneti ṣadasvṛkṣu catasṛṣvṛtubhiḥ saha | punardvayorṛtuneti bahutvaikatvalakṣitāḥ ||
3.d: तत्रर्तुनेति षदस्वृक्षु चतसृष्वृतुभिः सह | पुनर्द्वयोरृतुनेति बहुत्वैकत्वलक्षिताः ||
3.e: There (the deities) are characterized in the plural and in the singular, in six stanzas (1-6) 'with Rtu' (rtuna), in four with the Rtus (rtubhih), then again in two (11, 12) 'with Rtu'a.

3.s: ṛtavo devatābhiśca nipāteneha saṃstutāḥ | tathartupraiṣasūkte ca tathā gārtsamade'pi ca ||
3.d: ऋतवो देवताभिश्च निपातेनेह संस्तुताः | तथर्तुप्रैषसूक्ते च तथा गार्त्समदेऽपि च ||
3.e: The Rtus are here incidentally praised with the deities: so it is both in the hymn of summons (praisa) for offerings to the Rtus, and in the hymn of Grtsamada a also.

3.s: mukhyayā tvindramevāstaun marutastu dvitīyayā | tṛtīyayā tu tvaṣṭāraṃ caturthyā cāgnimeva ca ||
3.d: मुख्यया त्विन्द्रमेवास्तौन् मरुतस्तु द्वितीयया | तृतीयया तु त्वष्टारं चतुर्थ्या चाग्निमेव च ||
3.e: Now with the first (stanza) he (the seer) praised Indra, the Maruts with the second, Tvastrb with the third, and Agni with the fourth; caturthya cagnimeva ca

3.s: pañcamyā tu punaḥ śakraṃ ṣaṣṭyā devāvṛtāvṛdhau | saptamyādyābhiragniṃ ca caturbhirdraviṇodasam ||
3.d: पञ्चम्या तु पुनः शक्रं षष्ट्या देवावृतावृधौ | सप्तम्याद्याभिरग्निं च चतुर्भिर्द्रविणोदसम् ||

3.s: ādeśāddaivataṃ jñeyam ṛṅmantrāṇāṃ na liṅgataḥ | na śakyaṃ liṅgato hyāsāṃ jñātuṃ tattvena daivatam ||
3.d: आदेशाद्दैवतं ज्ञेयम् ऋङ्मन्त्राणां न लिङ्गतः | न शक्यं लिङ्गतो ह्यासां ज्ञातुं तत्त्वेन दैवतम् ||
3.e: The divinity of the formulas of the Rg-veda is to be known from authoritative statement (adesa), not from its characteristic mark (linga); for it is not possible to know actually (tattvena) the divinity of these (stanzas) from its characteristic mark. na

3.s: ekādaśyā tu nāsatyau dvādaśyāgnimimaṃ punaḥ | pṛthakpṛthakstutīdaṃ tu sūktamāha rathītaraḥ ||
3.d: एकादश्या तु नासत्यौ द्वादश्याग्निमिमं पुनः | पृथक्पृथक्स्तुतीदं तु सूक्तमाह रथीतरः ||
3.e: With the eleventh (he praises) the Nasatyas (Asvins), with the twelfth this Agni again. Rathitara, however, says that this hymn consists of single separate praises.

3.s: bahudaive dvidaive vā guṇairvā yatra karmajaiḥ | stūyate devataikaikā vibhaktastuti tadviduḥ ||
3.d: बहुदैवे द्विदैवे वा गुणैर्वा यत्र कर्मजैः | स्तूयते देवतैकैका विभक्तस्तुति तद्विदुः ||
3.e: For where, in (a hymn) with many deities or two deities, each deity is praised singly (ekaika) or by qualities arising from its activities, they regard that (hymn) as one containing distributed praisec (vibhakta-stuti).

3.s: vaiśvadevāni sūktāni trividhāni bhavanti tu | sūryasaṃstavasaṃyuktaṃ viśvaliṅgaṃ pṛthakstuti ||
3.d: वैश्वदेवानि सूक्तानि त्रिविधानि भवन्ति तु | सूर्यसंस्तवसंयुक्तं विश्वलिङ्गं पृथक्स्तुति ||
3.e: Now the hymns to the All-gods (vaisvadeva) are of three kinds that which is provided with joint-praise of the Sun (surya-samstava), that which contains the characteristic 'All' (visva-linga), and that which contains separate praise (prthak-stuti).

3.s: pṛthakstutīti yatproktaṃ tadvidyādbahudaivatam | viśvaliṅgaṃ tu tadyatra viśvaiḥ svaiḥ karmajairguṇaiḥ ||
3.d: पृथक्स्तुतीति यत्प्रोक्तं तद्विद्याद्बहुदैवतम् | विश्वलिङ्गं तु तद्यत्र विश्वैः स्वैः कर्मजैर्गुणैः ||
3.e: That which is called 'Separate praise' (prthak-stuti) one should recognize as addressed to many divinities; that which is characterized by All' (visva-linga) a is the one in which (the gods are praised) with their universal (visva) b qualities arising from their activities.

3.s: viśvānuddiśya yaddevān stauti sūryamanekadhā | devānevābhisaṃstauti taṃ prāhuḥ sūryasaṃstavam ||
3.d: विश्वानुद्दिश्य यद्देवान् स्तौति सूर्यमनेकधा | देवानेवाभिसंस्तौति तं प्राहुः सूर्यसंस्तवम् ||
3.e: That which with reference to the All-gods frequently praises the Sun, (and) at the same time praises the gods themselves, they call a joint-praise of the Sun (surya-samstava).

3.s: na tu bhāgasya sūktādau sakteṣvevauṣaseṣu vā | na sāvitre hrayāmīti na sūryāyāṃ kratau makhe ||
3.d: न तु भागस्य सूक्तादौ सक्तेष्वेवौषसेषु वा | न सावित्रे ह्रयामीति न सूर्यायां क्रतौ मखे ||
3.e: But (the term a does) not (apply) at the beginning of the hymn to Bhaga, nor in hymns to Usas, nor in the hymn to Savitr, 'I invoke' (hvayami: i. 35), nor in the Surya (hymn), in (regard to) oblation (and) sacrifice

3.s: na caivaivaṃ pravādeṣu mantreṣvanyeṣu keṣucit | na ca yatra sajoṣeti padaṃ vā syātsajūriti ||
3.d: न चैवैवं प्रवादेषु मन्त्रेष्वन्येषु केषुचित् | न च यत्र सजोषेति पदं वा स्यात्सजूरिति ||

3.s: yasminprasaṅgādapi tu bahvīnāṃ parikīrtanam | vaiśvadevaṃ tadapyāha sthaviro lāmakāyanaḥ ||
3.d: यस्मिन्प्रसङ्गादपि तु बह्वीनां परिकीर्तनम् | वैश्वदेवं तदप्याह स्थविरो लामकायनः ||
3.e: But the old Lamakayana a states even that (hymn) to be addressed to the All-gods, in which many (deities) are celebrated even incidentally (prasangat).

3.s: asaṃstutaṃ stutaṃ vāpi pradiṣṭaṃ daivataṃ kvacit | mantraistadṛṣayo'rcanti tāṃ tu budhyeta śāstravit ||
3.d: असंस्तुतं स्तुतं वापि प्रदिष्टं दैवतं क्वचित् | मन्त्रैस्तदृषयोऽर्चन्ति तां तु बुध्येत शास्त्रवित् ||
3.e: The divinity, whether praised or not, (but) indicated somewhere (in the hymn), the seers adore with formulas. That (deity) one learned in scripture (Sastra) should take note of.

3.s: ādau hi madhye cānte ca pṛthaktveṣu ca kartṛbhiḥ | karmāṇyanapadiṣṭāni pradiṣṭānyapi tu kvacit ||
3.d: आदौ हि मध्ये चान्ते च पृथक्त्वेषु च कर्तृभिः | कर्माण्यनपदिष्टानि प्रदिष्टान्यपि तु क्वचित् ||
3.e: For the actions (of the gods), though not designated by their agents, are nevertheless indicated b somewhere-at the beginning, and in the middle, and at the end, and in individual passages (prthaktvesu).

3.s: karmaiva tāvatsāvitryāṃ nividi stauti karmaṇā | yaddhenuḥ saptyanaḍvāhau voḻahā dogdhyāśureva vā ||
3.d: कर्मैव तावत्सावित्र्यां निविदि स्तौति कर्मणा | यद्धेनुः सप्त्यनड्वाहौ वोḻअहा दोग्ध्याशुरेव वा ||
3.e: The very action itself in the Nivid to Savitra praises by the action: since the cow, the courser, and the ox are (called) milker, swift, or carrier (C) (respectively). r.

3.s: bhāge yatstauti cāgnyādīn mitrādhīṃścāśvasaṃstutau | yadaibhiriti caitasmin vaiśva deve'gnimarcati ||
3.d: भागे यत्स्तौति चाग्न्यादीन् मित्राधींश्चाश्वसंस्तुतौ | यदैभिरिति चैतस्मिन् वैश्व देवेऽग्निमर्चति ||
3.e: Inasmuch as (the seer) praises Agni and others in the hymn to Bhaga (vii. 41), Mitra and others in the panegyric of the horse (i. 162), and adores Agni in (the hymn) to the All-gods, ' Hither with these' (aibhih, i. 14)

3.s: tadāhurādāvante ca prāyaśo'nyā stuvannṛcaḥ | pratiyogātprasaṅgādvā stautyanyāmapi devatām ||
3.d: तदाहुरादावन्ते च प्रायशोऽन्या स्तुवन्नृचः | प्रतियोगात्प्रसङ्गाद्वा स्तौत्यन्यामपि देवताम् ||

3.s: yasyāṃ vadatyarthavādān sā jñeyā sūktabhāginī | yāṃ tu stauti prasaṅgena sā vijñeyā nipātinī ||
3.d: यस्यां वदत्यर्थवादान् सा ज्ञेया सूक्तभागिनी | यां तु स्तौति प्रसङ्गेन सा विज्ञेया निपातिनी ||
3.e: The deity to whom he addresses statements of an object (arthavadan) a is to be known as hymn-owning (sukta-bhagini); but the one whom he praises on occasion (prasangena) is to be recognized as incidental (nipatini).

3.s: caturdhā bhaṇyate tasmin sūkte vā saktūbhāginī | pasminsarvāstu rājarṣīn ṛṣīnvāpi stuvannṛṣiḥ ||
3.d: चतुर्धा भण्यते तस्मिन् सूक्ते वा सक्तूभागिनी | पस्मिन्सर्वास्तु राजर्षीन् ऋषीन्वापि स्तुवन्नृषिः ||
3.e: In four ways (caturdha), it may be said (va), the hymnowning (deity) is mentioned (bhanyate) in that hymn in which a seer who praises all the royal Rishis or (divine) Rishis b is indicated (nirdista) r. ab

3.s: medhātithiragastyastu bṛhaduktho manurgayaḥ | ṛjiśvā vasukarṇaśca śāryāto gotamo luśaḥ ||
3.d: मेधातिथिरगस्त्यस्तु बृहदुक्थो मनुर्गयः | ऋजिश्वा वसुकर्णश्च शार्यातो गोतमो लुशः ||

3.s: svastyātreyaḥ parucchepaḥ kakṣīvān gāthinaurvaśau | nābhākaścaiva nirdiṣṭo duvasyurmamatāsutaḥ ||
