3.e: And two (stanzas, 13, 14, praise) Heaven and Earth; the stanza 'Soft' (syona: 15) should be held to be addressed to Earth. The (stanza) 'From thence' (atah: 16) is (addressed) optionally (va) to the gods; the rest of the hymn (17-21) a is addressed to Visnu.

3.s: vāyostīvrendravāyubhyāṃ dvṛco dvābhyāṃ tataḥ param | tṛco mitrāvaruṇayos tathendrāya marutvate ||
3.d: वायोस्तीव्रेन्द्रवायुभ्यां द्वृचो द्वाभ्यां ततः परम् | तृचो मित्रावरुणयोस् तथेन्द्राय मरुत्वते ||
3.e: To Vayu (belongs) 'Mighty' (tivrah: i. 23. 1); for the two, Indra-Vayu, there is a couplet (2, 3); after that there is a triplet to Mitra-Varuna (4-6), also (one) for Indra accompanied by the

3.s: tṛco viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ pūṣṇa āghṛṇaye tṛcaḥ | āsakto hi ghṛṇistasya dadhnaḥ pūrṇo dṛtī rathe ||
3.d: तृचो विश्वेषां देवानां पूष्ण आघृणये तृचः | आसक्तो हि घृणिस्तस्य दध्नः पूर्णो दृती रथे ||
3.e: (then) a triplet for the All-gods (10-12) and a triplet for Pusan Aghrni (13-15). B (He is thus named,) for there is attached (a-sakta) to his car a ghrni: a skin full of curds

3.s: āghṛṇistatstutaḥ pūṣā kīribhī ribhyate tataḥ | yathā hi madhunaḥ pūrṇo dṛtirarthyeti cāśvinau ||
3.d: आघृणिस्तत्स्तुतः पूषा कीरिभी रिभ्यते ततः | यथा हि मधुनः पूर्णो दृतिरर्थ्येति चाश्विनौ ||
3.e: Therefore (tat) he is praised as A-ghrni; hence he is lauded (ribhyate) by singers (kiri). For as their skin (drti) is full of mead, the suppliant (arthin) also approaches the Asvins (in the same way).

3.s: ā vartani madhuneti dṛtireva ca dṛśyate | ardhāṣṭamā apāṃ jñeyā adhyardhāntyāgnidevatā ||
3.d: आ वर्तनि मधुनेति दृतिरेव च दृश्यते | अर्धाष्टमा अपां ज्ञेया अध्यर्धान्त्याग्निदेवता ||
3.e: The skin itself appears in (the passage) 'Refresh the track with mead'a (a vartanim madhuna: iv. 45, 3°). Seven and a half (stanzas) are to be known as (belonging) to the Waters (16-23 ab); the last in addition to the (preceding) half (23 ed, 24) has Agni as its deity. a

3.s: kasya nūnaṃ tu kāryyādyā āgneyyṛk savitustṛcaḥ | bhagamaktasya bhāgī vā paraṃ yaccicca vāruṇam ||
3.d: कस्य नूनं तु कार्य्याद्या आग्नेय्यृक् सवितुस्तृचः | भगमक्तस्य भागी वा परं यच्चिच्च वारुणम् ||
3.e: But (in) 'Of whom now' (kasya nunam: i. 24) the first (stanza) is addressed to Ka (1), there is (then) a stanza addressed to Agni (2), a triplet (next) to Savitr (3-5), 'Bestowed by the gods' (bhaga-bhaktasya: 5), being optionally (va) addressed to Bhaga. What follows (6-15), as well as (the next hymn) 'Whatever' (yac cit: i. 25), is addressed to Varuna. i.

3.s: vasiṣvā hīti cāgneye ṛgagnermadhyamasya tu | jarābodheti vijñeyā vaiśvadevyuttamā namaḥ ||
3.d: वसिष्वा हीति चाग्नेये ऋगग्नेर्मध्यमस्य तु | जराबोधेति विज्ञेया वैश्वदेव्युत्तमा नमः ||
3.e: Do thou put on' (vasisva hi: i. 26) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni (26, 27); but the stanza 'Thou that knowest lauds' (jarabodha: i. 27. 10) is to be recognized as (belonging) to the Middle Agni; the last (stanza) 'Obeisance' (namah: i. 27. 13) is addressed to the All-gods. vaisvadevyuttama namah 4, vaisvadevyudgamah, vaisvadevyanamadgamah 1, vaisvadevyuttamottama 1. r.

3.s: parāścatasro yatreti indrolūkhalayo stutiḥ | manyete yāskakātthakyāv indrasyeti tu bhāguriḥ ||
3.d: पराश्चतस्रो यत्रेति इन्द्रोलूखलयो स्तुतिः | मन्येते यास्ककात्थक्याव् इन्द्रस्येति तु भागुरिः ||
3.e: The following four (stanzas), 'Where' (yatra: i. 28. 1-4), are (in) praise of Indra and the Mortar, (so) think Yaska a and Katthakya, but Bhaguri (thinks) of Indra (alone).

3.s: yacciddhyūlūkhalasya dve dve pare musalasya tu | carmādhiṣavaṇīyaṃ vā somaṃ vāntyā praśaṃsati ||
3.d: यच्चिद्ध्यूलूखलस्य द्वे द्वे परे मुसलस्य तु | चर्माधिषवणीयं वा सोमं वान्त्या प्रशंसति ||
3.e: 'If indeed' (yac cid dhi: i. 28. 5) a are two (stanzas in praise) of the Mortar (5, 6), the two following (7, 8) are (in praise) of the Pestle also; the last (stanza) lauds the skin used in pressing (adhisavaniya) or Soma.

3.s: aindra yacciddhi satyeti uttaraṃ cāśvinātṛcāt | āśvināduttaraḥ kasta uṣasyastṛca uttamaḥ ||
3.d: ऐन्द्र यच्चिद्धि सत्येति उत्तरं चाश्विनातृचात् | आश्विनादुत्तरः कस्त उषस्यस्तृच उत्तमः ||
3.e: 'What though, O True One' (yac cid dhi satya: i. 29) is addressed to Indra as well as the following (i. 30). After the 108 triplet Hither, O Asvins' (asvina: i. 30. 17-19), addressed to the Asvins, the next (uttara) triplet Who of thee' (kas te: 20-22), addressed to Dawn, is the last (triplet).

3.s: stūyamānaḥ śaśvaditi prītastu manasā dadau | śunaḥśepāya divyaṃ tu rathaṃ sarvaṃ hiraṇmayam ||
3.d: स्तूयमानः शश्वदिति प्रीतस्तु मनसा ददौ | शुनःशेपाय दिव्यं तु रथं सर्वं हिरण्मयम् ||
3.e: Being praised (with the stanza) 'For ever' (sasvat: i. 30. 16), he (Indra) a rejoiced in mind gave to Sunahsepa (the seer) a celestial car all made of gold.

3.s: āgneyaṃ yattvamaindre ca triścidityāśvinaṃ tataḥ | ṛte'rthavādaṃ karmaitad indrasyeti tu śaṃsati ||
3.d: आग्नेयं यत्त्वमैन्द्रे च त्रिश्चिदित्याश्विनं ततः | ऋतेऽर्थवादं कर्मैतद् इन्द्रस्येति तु शंसति ||
3.e: The (hymn) which (begins) Thou' (tvam: i. 31) is addressed to Agni; and (then come) two (32, 33) addressed to Indra. Then 'Even thrice' (tris cid: i. 34) is addressed to the Asvins; 'Of Indra' (indrasya: i. 32) lauds the action (of Indra) without (any) statement of an object (artha-vada). yatvam hrºfkr±rr 7, yattam, suktam r.

3.s: pādo'gnaye hvayāmīti maitrāvaruṇa uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo rātrisaṃstāvaḥ sūktaṃ sāvitramucyate ||
3.d: पादोऽग्नये ह्वयामीति मैत्रावरुण उत्तरः | तृतीयो रात्रिसंस्तावः सूक्तं सावित्रमुच्यते ||
3.e: (In) 'I invoke' (hvayami: i. 35) one verse (19) is to Agni, the next (1) is addressed to Mitra-Varuna, the third (1) is (in) praise of Night, (while) the (whole) hymn is stated to be addressed to Savitr. i.

3.s: pañcaitāni jagau dṛṣṭvā sūktānyāṅgiraso muni | hiraṇyastūpatāṃ prāpya sakhyaṃ cendreṇa śāśvatam ||
3.d: पञ्चैतानि जगौ दृष्ट्वा सूक्तान्याङ्गिरसो मुनि | हिरण्यस्तूपतां प्राप्य सख्यं चेन्द्रेण शाश्वतम् ||
3.e: These five hymns (31-35) a the sage, the son of Angiras, after he had seen them, sang, on gaining the position of Hiranyastupa and eternal friendship with Indra.

3.s: āgneyaṃ preti marutāṃ krīḻaṃ trīṇi parāṇyataḥ | uttiṣṭha brāhmaṇaspatyaṃ yaṃ rakṣanti trayastṛcāḥ ||
3.d: आग्नेयं प्रेति मरुतां क्रीḻअं त्रीणि पराण्यतः | उत्तिष्ठ ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं यं रक्षन्ति त्रयस्तृचाः ||
3.e: Forth' (pra: i. 36) is addressed to Agni; the three (37-39) following this (beginning) 'Sporting' (krilam: i. 37) are to the Maruts. 'Stand up' (ut tistha: i. 40) is addressed to Brahmanaspati. 'Whom they protect' (yam raksanti: i. 41) is (composed of) three

3.s: varuṇāryamamitrāṇāṃ madhyaṃ ādityadaivataḥ | pauṣṇaṃ saṃ pūṣanṣaḍraudryas tṛtīyā na tu kevalā ||
3.d: वरुणार्यममित्राणां मध्यं आदित्यदैवतः | पौष्णं सं पूषन्षड्रौद्र्यस् तृतीया न तु केवला ||
3.e: (the first, 1-3, and the third, 7-9, being addressed) to Varuna, Aryaman, and Mitra, (while) the middle one (4-6) has the Adityas for its divinities. Shorten, O Pusan' (sam pusan: i. 42) is addressed to Pusan. (Then come) six (stanzas) addressed to Rudra (i. 43. 1-6), the third, however, not exclusively.

3.s: mitreṇa varuṇenātra viśvedevaiśca saṃstavaḥ | uktamatrarṣiṇā pūrvam ādeśāddaivataṃ vinā ||
3.d: मित्रेण वरुणेनात्र विश्वेदेवैश्च संस्तवः | उक्तमत्रर्षिणा पूर्वम् आदेशाद्दैवतं विना ||
3.e: There is here (i. 43. 3) praise (of Rudra) along with Mitra, Varuna, and the All-gods. B It has already been said before a by the seer b that without an authoritative statement (adesa) the divinity

3.s: jñātuṃ na śakyate liṅgāt tathāpi kvaciducyate | ādityā vasavo rudrās tvamagna iti saṃstutāḥ ||
3.d: ज्ञातुं न शक्यते लिङ्गात् तथापि क्वचिदुच्यते | आदित्या वसवो रुद्रास् त्वमग्न इति संस्तुताः ||

3.s: tisraḥ saumyo'gna āgneye pragāthenāśvinau stutau | sahoṣasā liṅgabhājā ayaṃ soma sudānavaḥ ||
3.d: तिस्रः सौम्योऽग्न आग्नेये प्रगाथेनाश्विनौ स्तुतौ | सहोषसा लिङ्गभाजा अयं सोम सुदानवः ||
3.e: (Then come) three (stanzas) addressed to Soma (i. 43. 7-9). 'O Agni' (agne: i. 44. 1) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni (44, 45). With Pragatha couplet a the Asvins are (here) b praised with Dawn who bears her characteristic mark (linga-bhaj). 'Here is Soma, O bounteous ones' (ayam somah sudanavah: i. 45. 10ºd)

3.s: ardharco devadevasya eṣo ityāśvine pare | ādityaṃ manyate yāsko haviṣeti saha stutam ||
3.d: अर्धर्चो देवदेवस्य एषो इत्याश्विने परे | आदित्यं मन्यते यास्को हविषेति सह स्तुतम् ||

3.s: sahauṣase tataḥ sauryam udu tyamiti saṃstutaḥ | dyubhaktiryena varuṇo rogaghnastṛca uttamaḥ ||
3.d: सहौषसे ततः सौर्यम् उदु त्यमिति संस्तुतः | द्युभक्तिर्येन वरुणो रोगघ्नस्तृच उत्तमः ||
3.e: Together with' (saha: i. 48. 1) are two (hymns) addressed to Dawn (48, 49); then 'Upward him' (ud u tyam: i. 50) is addressed to Surya: (in) 'Wherewith' (yena: i. 50. 6) Varuna a connected with Heaven (dyubhakti) is praised; the last triplet (50. 11-13) is destructive of disease (rogaghna).

3.s: rogāpanuttirādyābhyām udyannisyuttame tṛce | ardharce tu dviṣaddveṣaḥ aindraḥ savyaḥ śatarciṣu ||
3.d: रोगापनुत्तिराद्याभ्याम् उद्यन्निस्युत्तमे तृचे | अर्धर्चे तु द्विषद्द्वेषः ऐन्द्रः सव्यः शतर्चिषु ||
3.e: With the first two (stanzas) in the last triplet (beginning) 'Rising' (udyan: i. 50. 11, 12) there is driving away of disease, while in a hemistich (of the last stanza) there is hostility to foes. Among the Satarcins is Savyad who is a form of Indra (aindra).

3.s: svayamindrasamaṃ putram icchato'ṅgiraso muneḥ | vajryeva savyo bhūtvarṣer yogitvātputratāṃ gataḥ ||
3.d: स्वयमिन्द्रसमं पुत्रम् इच्छतोऽङ्गिरसो मुनेः | वज्र्येव सव्यो भूत्वर्षेर् योगित्वात्पुत्रतां गतः ||
3.e: Of the sage Angiras who wished for a son like Indra, the Bolt-bearer himself became the sona, having assumed the form of Savya in consequence of the seer's asceticism.

3.s: prathame maṇḍale jñeyā ṛṣayastu śatarcinaḥ | kṣudrasūktamahāsūktā antye madhyeṣu madhyamāḥ ||
3.d: प्रथमे मण्डले ज्ञेया ऋषयस्तु शतर्चिनः | क्षुद्रसूक्तमहासूक्ता अन्त्ये मध्येषु मध्यमाः ||
3.e: Now the seers in the first book are to be known as Satarcins; in the last, as seers of short hymns and of long hymns; in the middle ones, as middlemen (madhyama).

3.s: navakaṃ jātavedasyaṃ nan cid yattu vayā iti | vaiśvānarīyaṃ tatsūktaṃ vahnimāgneyamuttaram ||
3.d: नवकं जातवेदस्यं नन् चिद् यत्तु वया इति | वैश्वानरीयं तत्सूक्तं वह्निमाग्नेयमुत्तरम् ||
3.e: 'Now indeed' (nu cit: i. 58), containing nine stanzas, is addressed to Jatavedas; while the hymn which (begins) 'Branches' (vayah i. 59) is addressed to Vaisvanara; the following one, 'Bearer' (vahnim: i. 60), is addressed to Agni. nu

3.s: aindrāṇyasmai tatastrīṇi vṛṣṇo śardhāya māratam | āgneyāni tu paśveti navaśaśvaddhi vāmiti ||
3.d: ऐन्द्राण्यस्मै ततस्त्रीणि वृष्णो शर्धाय मारतम् | आग्नेयानि तु पश्वेति नवशश्वद्धि वामिति ||
3.e: Then (come) three (61-63), 'To him' (asmai: i. 61), addressed to Indra; For the manly host' (vrsne sardhaya: i. 64) is addressed to the Maruts; 'With a cow' (pasva: i. 65) is (the first of) nine hymns (65-73) addressed to Agni; 'Ever indeed of you' (sasvad dhi vam)

3.s: daśāśvinānīmānīti indrāvaruṇayo stutiḥ | sauparṇeyāstu yāḥ kāścinnipātastutiṣu stutāḥ ||
3.d: दशाश्विनानीमानीति इन्द्रावरुणयो स्तुतिः | सौपर्णेयास्तु याः काश्चिन्निपातस्तुतिषु स्तुताः ||

3.s: upaprayantaḥ sūktāni āgneyānyuttarāṇi ṣaṭ | hiraṇyakeśo rajasaḥ tṛco'gnermadhyamasya tu ||
3.d: उपप्रयन्तः सूक्तानि आग्नेयान्युत्तराणि षट् | हिरण्यकेशो रजसः तृचोऽग्नेर्मध्यमस्य तु ||
3.e: The following six hymns (74-79), 'Going forth' (upaprayantah: i. 74. 1), are addressed to Agni ; but the triplet 'With golden locks, of air' (hiranyakeso rajasah: i. 79. 1-3) is (addressed) to the middle Agni.

3.s: ittheti pañca tvaindrāṇi yāmityasyāṃ nipātitāḥ | dadhyaṅ manuratharvā ca mārutāni pra ye tataḥ ||
3.d: इत्थेति पञ्च त्वैन्द्राणि यामित्यस्यां निपातिताः | दध्यङ् मनुरथर्वा च मारुतानि प्र ये ततः ||
3.e: Now 'Thus' (ittha: i. 80. 1) are five (80-84) addressed to Indra; in the (stanza) Whatever' (yam: i. 80. 16) Dadhyanc, Manu, and Atharvan are incidentally mentioned. Then They who forth' (pra ye: (pra ye: i. 85. 1) are addressed to the Maruts, II.

3.s: catvāryā no vaiśvadeve dve devānāṃ stutimate | ā no bhadrāśca devānāṃ bhadraṃ yāvacchataṃ punaḥ ||
3.d: चत्वार्या नो वैश्वदेवे द्वे देवानां स्तुतिमते | आ नो भद्राश्च देवानां भद्रं यावच्छतं पुनः ||

3.s: madhu vātāstṛce tasmin paramaṃ madhvapīṣyate | aditirdyauriti tvasyāṃ vibhūtiḥ kathitāditeḥ ||
3.d: मधु वातास्तृचे तस्मिन् परमं मध्वपीष्यते | अदितिर्द्यौरिति त्वस्यां विभूतिः कथितादितेः ||
3.e: In the triplet 'The winds waft mead' (madhu vatah: i. 90. 6) the supreme (parama) mead is also (api) a desired; but in the (stanza) Aditi is Heaven' (aditir dyauh: i. 89. 10) the majesty of Aditi is told.

3.s: tvaṃ saumyamauṣasam etā u tyāstṛco'śvinoḥ | aśvitāgneḥ sasomasya agnīṣomāviti stutiḥ ||
3.d: त्वं सौम्यमौषसम् एता उ त्यास्तृचोऽश्विनोः | अश्विताग्नेः ससोमस्य अग्नीषोमाविति स्तुतिः ||
3.e: 'Thou, Soma' (tvam soma: i. 91) is addressed to Soma; These Dawns' (eta u tyah: i. 92) is addressed to Dawn; the triplet O Asvins' (asvina: i. 92. 16-18), to the Asvins. Agni and Soma' (agnisomau: i. 93) is (in) praise of Agni associated with Soma. i.

3.s: gotamādauśijaḥ kutsaḥ parucchepādṛṣeḥ paraḥ | kutsaddīrghatamāḥ śaśvat te dve evamadhīyate ||
3.d: गोतमादौशिजः कुत्सः परुच्छेपादृषेः परः | कुत्सद्दीर्घतमाः शश्वत् ते द्वे एवमधीयते ||
3.e: After Gotama (74-93) the son of Usij (Kaksivat comes: 116-126); after the seer Paruchepa (127-139) follows Kutsa (94-115); after Kutsa, Dirghatamasa (140-164): always (sasvat) these twob (sets respectively); in this order (evam) is read (the text of the Rg-veda).

3.s: imaṃ kutsa āṅgiraso dadarśa jātavedasyaṃ jagāda ṣoḻaśarcam | pūrvo devā ityṛco devadevās trayaḥ pādā uttamāyāstato'rdham ||
3.d: इमं कुत्स आङ्गिरसो ददर्श जातवेदस्यं जगाद षोḻअशर्चम् | पूर्वो देवा इत्यृचो देवदेवास् त्रयः पादा उत्तमायास्ततोऽर्धम् ||
3.e: Kutsa, son of Angiras, saw 'This' (imam: i. 94): he uttered (this hymn) containing sixteen stanzas (and) addressed to Jatavedas. A Three verses (8 abc) of the stanza Foremost, O Gods' (purvo devah: i. 94. 8) have the gods as their deities; then half of the last (stanza: i. 94. 16)

3.s: tasyaiva vā yasya tatpūrvasūktaṃ mitrā- dibhyo vātra ṣaḍbhyaḥ prakṛtābhyaḥ | antyo'rdharcastu vā ṣaṇṇāṃ stutānāṃ pūrvo devāḥ pādastu tribhi stutāḥ ||
3.d: तस्यैव वा यस्य तत्पूर्वसूक्तं मित्रा- दिभ्यो वात्र षड्भ्यः प्रकृताभ्यः | अन्त्योऽर्धर्चस्तु वा षण्णां स्तुतानां पूर्वो देवाः पादस्तु त्रिभि स्तुताः ||

3.s: bharadvāje gṛtsamade vasiṣṭhe nodhasyagastye vimade nabhāke | kutse nodarkā bahudaivateṣu tathā dvideveṣu samānadharmiṇaḥ ||
3.d: भरद्वाजे गृत्समदे वसिष्ठे नोधस्यगस्त्ये विमदे नभाके | कुत्से नोदर्का बहुदैवतेषु तथा द्विदेवेषु समानधर्मिणः ||

3.s: dve virūpe sūktamauṣasāyāgnaye sa pratnatheti draviṇodase'gnaye | vaiśvānarasyeti vaiśvānarīyam asmātpūrvaṃ śucaye'gnaye punaḥ ||
3.d: द्वे विरूपे सूक्तमौषसायाग्नये स प्रत्नथेति द्रविणोदसेऽग्नये | वैश्वानरस्येति वैश्वानरीयम् अस्मात्पूर्वं शुचयेऽग्नये पुनः ||
3.e: Two unlike' (dve virupe: i. 95) is a hymn to Agni Ausasa, 'He in the ancient way' (sa pratnatha: i. 96) is to Agni Dravinodas, 'Of Vaisvanara' (vaisvanarasya: i. 98) is addressed to Vaisvanara; but the one before this (i. 97) is to Agni Suci.

3.s: jātavedasyaṃ sūktasahasrameka aindrātpūrvaṃ kaśyapārṣaṃ vadanti | jātavedase sūktamādyaṃ tu teṣām ekabhūyastvaṃ manyate śākapūṇiḥ ||
3.d: जातवेदस्यं सूक्तसहस्रमेक ऐन्द्रात्पूर्वं कश्यपार्षं वदन्ति | जातवेदसे सूक्तमाद्यं तु तेषाम् एकभूयस्त्वं मन्यते शाकपूणिः ||
3.e: Some say that the thousand hymns addressed to Jatavedas (which come) before (the hymn) addressed to Indra (i. 100) have Kasyapa as their seera: the first hymn of these is 'For Jatavedas' (jatavedase: i. 99). Sakapuni thinks that they increase by one (in the number of their stanzas).

3.s: sa yo vṛṣaindrāṇi pañca vaiśvadevāni candramāḥ | trīṇyaindrāgne ya indrāgnī tatamityārbhave pare ||
3.d: स यो वृषैन्द्राणि पञ्च वैश्वदेवानि चन्द्रमाः | त्रीण्यैन्द्राग्ने य इन्द्राग्नी ततमित्यार्भवे परे ||
3.e: The mighty one who' (sa yo vrsa: i. 100) is (the first of) five (hymns) addressed to Indra (100-104); there are (then) three (105-107) addressed to the All-gods, (beginning) 'The Moon' (candramas: i. 105. 1). 'That which, O Indra-Agni' (ya indragni: i. 108) is (the first of) two addressed to Indra-Agni (108, 109); the two following (110, 111) 'I wrought' (tatam: i. 110. 1) are addressed to the Rbhus.

3.s: tritaṃ gāstvanugacchantaṃ krūrā sālāvṛkīsutāḥ | kūpe prakṣipya gāḥ sarvās tata evāpajahrire ||
3.d: त्रितं गास्त्वनुगच्छन्तं क्रूरा सालावृकीसुताः | कूपे प्रक्षिप्य गाः सर्वास् तत एवापजह्रिरे ||
3.e: The cruel sons of the she-wolf (salavrki) a having cast Trita, who was following the cows, into a well, carried off all the cows from thence.

3.s: sa tatra suṣuve somaṃ mantravinmantravittamaḥ | devāṃścāvāhayatsarvāṃs tacchuśrāva bṛhaspatiḥ ||
3.d: स तत्र सुषुवे सोमं मन्त्रविन्मन्त्रवित्तमः | देवांश्चावाहयत्सर्वांस् तच्छुश्राव बृहस्पतिः ||
3.e: He, the best knower of formulas among all knowers of such, pressed Soma there and summoned all the gods: Brhaspati heard that (call). sa

3.s: āgacchato'tha tāndṛṣṭvā kva vasatyasya tattvataḥ | sarvadṛktvaṃ ca varuṇasyāryamṇaścetyupālabhat ||
3.d: आगच्छतोऽथ तान्दृष्ट्वा क्व वसत्यस्य तत्त्वतः | सर्वदृक्त्वं च वरुणस्यार्यम्णश्चेत्युपालभत् ||
3.e: Now on seeing them coming, he reproached (them), saying, 'Where, indeed, abides, the all-seeing power (sarvadrktva) of this Varuna and of Aryaman?

3.s: kūpeṣṭakābhirvraṇitāny saṅgānyevābhayanmama | dṛṣṭvā sarvānahaṃ staumi yadyapyeko na paśyati ||
3.d: कूपेष्टकाभिर्व्रणितान्य् सङ्गान्येवाभयन्मम | दृष्ट्वा सर्वानहं स्तौमि यद्यप्येको न पश्यति ||
3.e: 'My limbs were wounded by the bricks of the well. Having seen all (the gods) I praise (them), even though not one (of them) sees (me).'

3.s: bṛhaspatipracoditā viśvedevagaṇāstrayaḥ | jagmustritasya taṃ yajñaṃ bhāgāṃśca jagṛhuḥ saha ||
3.d: बृहस्पतिप्रचोदिता विश्वेदेवगणास्त्रयः | जग्मुस्त्रितस्य तं यज्ञं भागांश्च जगृहुः सह ||
3.e: The three troops a of the All-gods, urged on by Brhaspati, went to that sacrifice of Trita and took shares of it together.

3.s: bṛhaspatistritasyaitaj jñānaṃ vijñānameva ca | tṛcenāntyena sūktasya jagādarṣirasāviti ||
3.d: बृहस्पतिस्त्रितस्यैतज् ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च | तृचेनान्त्येन सूक्तस्य जगादर्षिरसाविति ||
3.e: As a seer Brhaspati declared the knowledge and discernment of Trita here displayed (etat) with the last triplet (i. 105. 16-18)a of the hymn (beginning) 'That' (asau: i. 105. 16).

3.s: dyāvāpṛthivyorīḻeti āgneyaḥ pāda uttaraḥ | āśvinaḥ sūktaśeṣaḥ syāda idaṃ rātryuṣaso stutiḥ ||
3.d: द्यावापृथिव्योरीḻएति आग्नेयः पाद उत्तरः | आश्विनः सूक्तशेषः स्याद इदं रात्र्युषसो स्तुतिः ||
3.e: (The verse) 'I praise' (ile: i. 112. 1) is to Heaven and Earth, the next verse (1) is addressed to Agni ; the remainder of the hymn (112. 1 cd-25) should be (regarded as) addressed to the Asvinsa. 'This' (idam: i. 113) is (in) praise of Night and Dawn. I

3.s: imā raudraṃ paraṃ sauryaṃ citraṃ paścāśvinānyataḥ | nāsatyābhyāmiti tvantye antyā duḥsvapnanāśino ||
3.d: इमा रौद्रं परं सौर्यं चित्रं पश्चाश्विनान्यतः | नासत्याभ्यामिति त्वन्त्ये अन्त्या दुःस्वप्ननाशिनो ||
3.e: 'These' (imah: i. 114) is addressed to Rudra; the next, 'The brilliant' (citram: i. 115), is addressed to the Sun. Then 120 (come) five (i. 116-120) addressed to the Asvins (beginning) 'For the Nasatyas' (nasatyabhyam: i. 116. 1): the last (stanza) in the last (hymn i. 120. 12) is destructive of evil dreams.

3.s: aindraṃ kadvaiśvadevaṃ ca prauṣase pṛthuruttare | ṛṣirdānaṃ ca bhāvyasya prātarityatra śaṃsati ||
3.d: ऐन्द्रं कद्वैश्वदेवं च प्रौषसे पृथुरुत्तरे | ऋषिर्दानं च भाव्यस्य प्रातरित्यत्र शंसति ||
3.e: When?' (kad: i. 121) is addressed to Indra, and 'Forth' (pra: i. 122) is addressed to the All-gods. The two (123, 124) next (beginning) 'Broad' (prthuh: i. 123. 1) are addressed to Dawn (ausase). In 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125) the seer lauds the gift of Bhavyaa.

3.s: kākṣīvataṃ kadittheti yadaindramupadiśyate | parokṣaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tat pradiṣṭaṃ svarasāmasu ||
3.d: काक्षीवतं कदित्थेति यदैन्द्रमुपदिश्यते | परोक्षं वैश्वदेवं तत् प्रदिष्टं स्वरसामसु ||
3.e: 'When, indeed?' (kad ittha: i. 121), a hymn of Kaksivat which is traditionally held to be addressed to Indra, is indicated as indirectly addressed (paroksa) to the All-gods in the Svarasamansa.

3.s: adhigamya gurorvidyāṃ gacchansvanilayaṃ kila | kakṣīvānadhvani śrāntaḥ suṣvāpāraṇyagocaraḥ ||
3.d: अधिगम्य गुरोर्विद्यां गच्छन्स्वनिलयं किल | कक्षीवानध्वनि श्रान्तः सुष्वापारण्यगोचरः ||
3.e: Having acquired knowledge from his spiritual teacher (and) going home, as we are told (kila), Kaksivat fatigued on the way fell asleep within the forest.

3.s: taṃ rājā svanayo nāma bhāvayavyasuto vrajan | krīḍārthaṃ sānugo'paśyat sabhāryaḥ sapurohitaḥ ||
3.d: तं राजा स्वनयो नाम भावयव्यसुतो व्रजन् | क्रीडार्थं सानुगोऽपश्यत् सभार्यः सपुरोहितः ||
3.e: Him a king, Svanaya by name, the son of Bhavayavya, saw as he went along to amuse himself, accompanied by his retinue, his wife, and his domestic priest. bhavayavyasuto hm`rn (d), bhavayavyastuto, bhavayavyastato fkr'n (ab). The reading °suto is supported by Sayana (on Rg-veda i. 125. 1, where the story of Kaksivat is told), who calls Svanaya bhavayavyasya putrah | . - The unanimity of the MSS. in writing kridartham has caused a lapse from consistency, which requires in the text.

3.s: athainaṃ rūpasaṃpannaṃ dṛṣṭvā devasutopamam | kanyādāne matiṃ cakre varṇagotrāvirodhataḥ ||
3.d: अथैनं रूपसंपन्नं दृष्ट्वा देवसुतोपमम् | कन्यादाने मतिं चक्रे वर्णगोत्राविरोधतः ||
3.e: Then on seeing him endowed with beauty (and) resembling the son of a god, he thought of bestowing his daughter (on him), if there were no objection on the score of caste and family.

3.s: saṃbodhyainaṃ sa papraccha varṇagotrādikaṃ tataḥ | rājannāṅgiraso'smīti kumāraḥ pratyuvāca tam ||
3.d: संबोध्यैनं स पप्रच्छ वर्णगोत्रादिकं ततः | राजन्नाङ्गिरसोऽस्मीति कुमारः प्रत्युवाच तम् ||
3.e: Then after wakening him he inquired as to his caste, family, and so forth. The youth replied to him saying, 'O king, I am of the race of Angiras; cd:

3.s: putro'haṃ dīrghatamasa aucathyasya ṛṣernṛpa | athāsmai sa dadau kanyā daśābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ ||
3.d: पुत्रोऽहं दीर्घतमस औचथ्यस्य ऋषेर्नृप | अथास्मै स ददौ कन्या दशाभरणभूषिताः ||
3.e: A similar distinction between dhana and kupya is found in Manu vii. 96. There is no reference to these, nor to sheep and goats, in the text of the hymn.

3.s: tāvataśca rathāñchyāvān vīḍvaṅgānvai caturyujaḥ | vadhūnāṃ vāhanārthāya dhanakupyamajāvikam ||
3.d: तावतश्च रथाञ्छ्यावान् वीड्वङ्गान्वै चतुर्युजः | वधूनां वाहनार्थाय धनकुप्यमजाविकम् ||

3.s: niṣkāṇāṃ vṛṣabhāṇāṃ ca śataṃ śatamadātpunaḥ | etaduttarasūktena śatamityādinoditam ||
3.d: निष्काणां वृषभाणां च शतं शतमदात्पुनः | एतदुत्तरसूक्तेन शतमित्यादिनोदितम् ||
3.e: Further he gave (him) a hundred necklets and a hundred bulls. This is told in the next hymn with (the stanza) A hundred' (satam: i. 126. 2) and so forth.

3.s: śatamaśvāñchataṃ niṣkān rathāndaśa vadhūmataḥ | caturyujo gavāṃ caiva sahasraṃ ṣaṣṭhyupādhikam ||
3.d: शतमश्वाञ्छतं निष्कान् रथान्दश वधूमतः | चतुर्युजो गवां चैव सहस्रं षष्ठ्युपाधिकम् ||
3.e: A hundred horses, a hundred necklets, ten chariots with maidens, (steeds) going in teams of four, and a thousand and sixty cows

3.s: svanayādbhāvayavyādyaḥ kakṣīvānpratyapadyata | pratigṛhya ca tuṣṭāva prātaḥ pitre śaśaṃsa ca ||
3.d: स्वनयाद्भावयव्याद्यः कक्षीवान्प्रत्यपद्यत | प्रतिगृह्य च तुष्टाव प्रातः पित्रे शशंस च ||
3.e: Kaksivat, who obtained (all this) from Svanaya Bhavayavya, both praised (him) after receiving (it) and recited (the hymn) 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125) to his father. i.

3.s: phalapradarśanaṃ tasya kriyate prāyaśastviha | dvitīyāṃ tu pitāpaśyat sugurityādikāmṛcam ||
3.d: फलप्रदर्शनं तस्य क्रियते प्रायशस्त्विह | द्वितीयां तु पितापश्यत् सुगुरित्यादिकामृचम् ||
3.e: Now here (in 125) the rewards (of liberality) are for the most part set forth to him. The father, however, saw the second (stanza), which begins Possessed of many kine' (suguh: 125. 2). The three slokas 151-153 are found in

3.s: kākṣīvataṃ sarvamiti bhagavānāha śaunakaḥ | eṣā tu dairghatamasī sānuliṅgā kathaṃ bhavet ||
3.d: काक्षीवतं सर्वमिति भगवानाह शौनकः | एषा तु दैर्घतमसी सानुलिङ्गा कथं भवेत् ||
3.e: The revered Saunaka says that the whole (hymn) is Kaksivat's. But as to this (stanza), how could it, according to the indications (it contains), have been seen by

3.s: ucyate prātarityukte sūnordānena harṣitaḥ | rājñaścāśiṣamāhātha sugurityādinā kila ||
3.d: उच्यते प्रातरित्युक्ते सूनोर्दानेन हर्षितः | राज्ञश्चाशिषमाहाथ सुगुरित्यादिना किल ||
3.e: The answer is, that when 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125. 1) had been uttered (by Kaksivat), he (Dirghatamas) was delighted by the gift to his son, and then uttered a prayer for the king with (the stanza) 'Possessed of many kine' (suguh: i. 125. 2).

3.s: karmāṇi yābhiḥ kathitāni rājñāṃ dānāni coccāvacamadhyamāni | nārāśaṃsīrityṛcastāḥ pratīyād yābhi stutirdāśatayīṣu rājñām ||
3.d: कर्माणि याभिः कथितानि राज्ञां दानानि चोच्चावचमध्यमानि | नाराशंसीरित्यृचस्ताः प्रतीयाद् याभि स्तुतिर्दाशतयीषु राज्ञाम् ||
3.e: The stanzas in which the deeds of kings and their gifts, great, small, and middling, are told, should be understood to be called Laudations of Men' (narasamsi), as the praise of kings (is expressed) by them in the ten books (of the Rg-veda).

3.s: pañcāmandānbhāvayavyasya gītā jāyāpatyoḥ saṃpravādo dvṛcena | saṃpravādaṃ romaśayendrarājñora ete ṛcau manyate śākapūṇiḥ ||
3.d: पञ्चामन्दान्भावयव्यस्य गीता जायापत्योः संप्रवादो द्वृचेन | संप्रवादं रोमशयेन्द्रराज्ञोर एते ऋचौ मन्यते शाकपूणिः ||
3.e: The five (stanzas) 'Lively' (amandan : 1. 126. 1-5) are a song (in praise) of Bhavayavya. With a couplet (6, 7) there is a conversation of a husband and wife. Sakapuni thinks these two stanzas are a conversation of Indra and the king with Romasa.

3.s: indre jāyāpatyoścetihāsaṃ dvṛce'sminmanyate śākaṭāyanaḥ | prādātsutāṃ romaśāṃ nāma nāmnā bṛhaspatirbhāvayavyāya rājño ||
3.d: इन्द्रे जायापत्योश्चेतिहासं द्वृचेऽस्मिन्मन्यते शाकटायनः | प्रादात्सुतां रोमशां नाम नाम्ना बृहस्पतिर्भावयव्याय राज्ञो ||
3.e: Sakatayana thinks that in this couplet there is a story of a husband and wife (in connexion) with Indra. Brhaspati gave his daughter, Romasa by name, to king Bhavayavya. r.

4.s: tatastamarthaṃ harivānviditvā priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ svanayaṃ didṛkṣuḥ | abhyājagāmāśu śacīsahāyaḥ prītyārcayattaṃ vidhinaiva rājā ||
4.d: ततस्तमर्थं हरिवान्विदित्वा प्रियं सखायं स्वनयं दिदृक्षुः | अभ्याजगामाशु शचीसहायः प्रीत्यार्चयत्तं विधिनैव राजा ||
4.e: Then the Lord of Bays, the Companion of Saci (Indra) becoming aware of that affair, (and) desirous of seeing his dear friend Svanaya, quickly went to him. him with due ceremony. The king joyfully

4.s: abhyājagāmāṅgirasī ca tatra hṛṣṭā tayoḥ sā caraṇau vavande | indraḥ sakhitvādatha tāmuvāca romāṇi te santi na santi rājñi ||
4.d: अभ्याजगामाङ्गिरसी च तत्र हृष्टा तयोः सा चरणौ ववन्दे | इन्द्रः सखित्वादथ तामुवाच रोमाणि ते सन्ति न सन्ति राज्ञि ||
4.e: And the daughter of the Angiras (Brhaspati) came there: rejoicing she adored their feet. Indra then in a friendly way said to her, 'Have you hair or have you not, O Queen?'

4.s: sā bālabhāvādatha taṃ jagāda upopa me śakra parāmṛśeti | tāṃ pūrvayā sāntvya nṛpaḥ prahṛṣṭo anvavrajatsātha patiṃ pativratāṃ ||
4.d: सा बालभावादथ तं जगाद उपोप मे शक्र परामृशेति | तां पूर्वया सान्त्व्य नृपः प्रहृष्टो अन्वव्रजत्साथ पतिं पतिव्रतां ||
4.e: She in a childlike way then addressed him, 'Feel me closely (upopa me: i. 126. 7), Mighty One'a. The king having soothed her with the previous (stanza: i. 126. 6), rejoiced. She then followed her husband as a devoted wife. r.

4.s: athāgneye agnimityuttare yaṃ pañcaindrāṇi pra tadaindavyṛgatra | śaṃ tamindrāparvatau saha stutau tvindraṃ mena iha yāskaḥ pradhānam ||
4.d: अथाग्नेये अग्निमित्युत्तरे यं पञ्चैन्द्राणि प्र तदैन्दव्यृगत्र | शं तमिन्द्रापर्वतौ सह स्तुतौ त्विन्द्रं मेन इह यास्कः प्रधानम् ||
4.e: Next follow two hymns (127, 128) addressed to Agni (beginning) 'Agni' (agnim: i. 127). There are (then) five (129- 133) addressed to Indra (beginning) Which' (yam: i. 129). Here the stanza 'Forth this' (pra tad: i. 129. 6) is addressed to Indu, while Indra-Parvata are praised together (in) 'Ye him' (yuvam tam: i. 132. 6). Yaska here considered Indra to be predominant.

4.s: ṛkṣu stutaḥ parvatavaddhi vajro dvivatstutau cendramāhuḥ pradhānam | ā tvā vāyonava pañcendravāyvor ekā vāyoruttaraṃ dvipradhānam ||
4.d: ऋक्षु स्तुतः पर्वतवद्धि वज्रो द्विवत्स्तुतौ चेन्द्रमाहुः प्रधानम् | आ त्वा वायोनव पञ्चेन्द्रवाय्वोर् एका वायोरुत्तरं द्विप्रधानम् ||
4.e: For in (certain) stanzas (Indra's) bolt is praised as Parvata, and when there is praise (of the two) in the dual (dvivat-stutau) they say that Indra is predominant. (Beginning with) 'Hither thee' (a tva: i. 134. 1) there are nine (stanzas: i. 134. 1-6, 135. 1-3) to Vayu, (then) five (i. 135. 4-8) to Indra-Vayu, (then) one (i. 135. 9) to Vayu. The next (hymn: i. 136) has two predominant (deities).

4.s: tatra pañca varuṇamitradevā divādibhyaḥ kathitābhyaḥ pare dve | dve dve pade saṃstute rodasī ca devāścārdharcena vibhaktamanyat ||
4.d: तत्र पञ्च वरुणमित्रदेवा दिवादिभ्यः कथिताभ्यः परे द्वे | द्वे द्वे पदे संस्तुते रोदसी च देवाश्चार्धर्चेन विभक्तमन्यत् ||
4.e: There five (stanzas: i. 136. 1-5) have Varuna and Mitra for their gods; the following two (i. 136. 6, 7) are (addressed) to the (deities) mentioned, Dyaus and the rest. Couples (of deities: dve dve), including the Two Worlds (rodasi), are praised together (samstute), (each) in a verse (pada), and the gods (are praised) with a hemistich (7); the rest (7 cd) is distributed (in praise). C r.

4.s: maitrāvaruṇaṃ suṣumeti sūktaṃ prapra pauṣṇaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyam | astu śrauṣaḍ vaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ syādbahudevateṣu ||
4.d: मैत्रावरुणं सुषुमेति सूक्तं प्रप्र पौष्णं वैश्वदेवं तृतीयम् | अस्तु श्रौषड् वैश्वदेवं तृतीयं वैश्वदेवं स्याद्बहुदेवतेषु ||
4.e: The hymn 'We have pressed' (i. 137) is addressed to MitraVaruna. Forth, forth' (pra-pra: i. 138) is addressed to Pusan, the third (i. 139) is addressed to the All-gods. 'Let it be heard' (astu srausat: i. 139) is the third hymn addressed to the All-gods. A hymn to the All-gods may be (included) among those which contain many deities.

4.s: bahuśastu vaiśvadeveṣu santyṛcaḥ pādārdharcā dvaipadāstraipadāśca | dvipradhānā api caikapradhānā bahupradhānā api vaiśvadevāḥ ||
4.d: बहुशस्तु वैश्वदेवेषु सन्त्यृचः पादार्धर्चा द्वैपदास्त्रैपदाश्च | द्विप्रधाना अपि चैकप्रधाना बहुप्रधाना अपि वैश्वदेवाः ||
4.e: There are variously (bahusah), in (hymns) addressed to the All-gods, stanzas, verses, hemistichsa, stanzas with two verses (dvaipadah) or with three (traipadah): (such) Vaisvadeva (formulas) have two predominant (deities) or one predominant (deity) or many predominant (deities).

4.s: vaiśvadevī maitrāvaruṇī dvitīyā tisro'śvibhyāṃ tata aindrī tato'gneḥ | mārutyekā tata aindrāgnyanantarā bārhaspatyā cottamā stauti devān ||
4.d: वैश्वदेवी मैत्रावरुणी द्वितीया तिस्रोऽश्विभ्यां तत ऐन्द्री ततोऽग्नेः | मारुत्येका तत ऐन्द्राग्न्यनन्तरा बार्हस्पत्या चोत्तमा स्तौति देवान् ||
4.e: There is (one: i. 139. 1) addressed to the All-gods, the second (2) is addressed to Mitra -Varuna; three (3-5) are to the Asvins, then (one) is addressed to Indra (6), then (one) to Agni (7), one is addressed to the Maruts (8), then (one) is addressed to Indra-Agni (9); and the next is addressed to Brhaspati (10); the last (stanza) praises the gods (11).

4.s: ṛṣīnṛṣirvā stauti dadhyaṅha me'syām ātmānaṃ vā teṣu śaṃsansvajanma | tasmādasyāṃ vipravadanti kecid indrāgnī tasyāṃ tu nipātabhājau ||
4.d: ऋषीनृषिर्वा स्तौति दध्यङ्ह मेऽस्याम् आत्मानं वा तेषु शंसन्स्वजन्म | तस्मादस्यां विप्रवदन्ति केचिद् इन्द्राग्नी तस्यां तु निपातभाजौ ||
4.e: The seer in the (stanza) 'Dadhyanc of me' (dadhyan ha me: i. 139. 9) praises either the (ancient) seers or himself a by 128 some proclaiming his own origin among them. For this reason b disagree in regard to this (stanza, saying), that Indra-Agni are at the same time (tu) incidentally praised (nipata-bhaj) in it.

4.s: dvāvucathyabṛhaspatī ṛṣiputrau babhūvatuḥ | āsīducathyabhāryā tu mamatā nāma bhārgavī ||
4.d: द्वावुचथ्यबृहस्पती ऋषिपुत्रौ बभूवतुः | आसीदुचथ्यभार्या तु ममता नाम भार्गवी ||
4.e: There were (once) two seers' sons, Ucathya and Brhaspati. Now Ucathya's wife was Mamata by name, of the race of Bhrgu.

4.s: tāṃ kanīyānbṛhaspatir maithunāyopacakrame | śukrasyotsargakāle tu garbhastaṃ pratyabhāṣata ||
4.d: तां कनीयान्बृहस्पतिर् मैथुनायोपचक्रमे | शुक्रस्योत्सर्गकाले तु गर्भस्तं प्रत्यभाषत ||
4.e: Brhaspati, the younger (of the two), approached her for sexual intercourse. Now at the time of impregnation the embryo addressed him:

4.s: ihāsmi pūrvasaṃbhūto na kāryaḥ śukrasaṃkaraḥ | tacchrukrapratiṣedhaṃ tu na mamarṣa bṛhaspatiḥ ||
4.d: इहास्मि पूर्वसंभूतो न कार्यः शुक्रसंकरः | तच्छ्रुक्रप्रतिषेधं तु न ममर्ष बृहस्पतिः ||
4.e: 'Here am I previously engendered; you must not cause a commingling of seed.' Brhaspati, however, could not brook this remonstrance about the seed.

4.s: sa vyājahāra taṃ garbhaṃ tamaste dīrghamastviti | sa ca dīrghatamā nāma babhūvarṣirucathyajaḥ ||
4.d: स व्याजहार तं गर्भं तमस्ते दीर्घमस्त्विति | स च दीर्घतमा नाम बभूवर्षिरुचथ्यजः ||
4.e: (So) he addressed the embryo: 'Long darkness shall be your lot.' And (hence) the seer, Ucathya's son, was born with the name Dirghatamas (Long Darkness). tam

4.s: sa jāto'bhyatapaddevān akasmādandhatāṃ gataḥ | dadurdevāstu tannetre tato'nandho babhūva saḥ ||
4.d: स जातोऽभ्यतपद्देवान् अकस्मादन्धतां गतः | ददुर्देवास्तु तन्नेत्रे ततोऽनन्धो बभूव सः ||
4.e: He when born distressed the gods, having become suddenly blind. The gods, however, gave him (the use of) his eyes (tannetre); so he was cured of his blindness.

4.s: sa vediṣada ityastoc caturbhirjātavedasam | samiddha āpriyo'ntyaindro tamityagneḥ parāṇi ṣaṭ ||
4.d: स वेदिषद इत्यस्तोच् चतुर्भिर्जातवेदसम् | समिद्ध आप्रियोऽन्त्यैन्द्रो तमित्यग्नेः पराणि षट् ||
4.e: With four (hymns beginning) 'To him seated on the altar' (vedisade: i. 140) he praised Jatavedas (Agni). 'Kindled' (samiddhah: i. 142) is an Apri hymn, its last (stanza) being addressed to Indra (i. 142. 13). The six (i. 145-150) following (beginning) 'Him' (tam: i. 145. 1) are to Agni.

4.s: stutau tu mitrāvaruṇau sūktairmitramiti tribhiḥ | mitraṃ maitrīṃ vadanyetām ā dhenavaśca śaṃsati ||
4.d: स्तुतौ तु मित्रावरुणौ सूक्तैर्मित्रमिति त्रिभिः | मित्रं मैत्रीं वदन्येताम् आ धेनवश्च शंसति ||
4.e: But Mitra-Varuna are praised with the three (151-153) hymns (beginning) 'A Friend' (mitram: i. 151). 'A Friend (mitram: i. 151. 1) expresses that this (stanza) is addressed to Mitra (only). May the kine' (a dhenavah: i. 152. 6)

4.s: aditiṃ vāthavāpyagniṃ tathā rūpaṃ hi dṛśyate | agniṃ mene'ditiṃ tveva kutse ceha ca śaunakaḥ ||
4.d: अदितिं वाथवाप्यग्निं तथा रूपं हि दृश्यते | अग्निं मेनेऽदितिं त्वेव कुत्से चेह च शौनकः ||

4.s: ṛṣiratra prasaṅgādvā darśanādvānukīrtayet | biṣṇornu kamiti trīṇi vaiṣṇavāni parāṇyataḥ ||
4.d: ऋषिरत्र प्रसङ्गाद्वा दर्शनाद्वानुकीर्तयेत् | बिष्णोर्नु कमिति त्रीणि वैष्णवानि पराण्यतः ||
4.e: The seer may here mention (Aditi) either incidentally (prasangat) or because he saw (Agni in this form). The three (hymns) after this (i. 154-156), (beginning) Of Visnu now' (visnor nu kam i. 154. 1), are addressed to Visnu; The reading of 19 ab in the text is that of

4.s: pra vaśca tisṛbhirṛgbhir indrāviṣṇu saha stutau | gṛhāṇi vā vaiṣṇavāni tā vāmityṛci kāṅkṣati ||
4.d: प्र वश्च तिसृभिरृग्भिर् इन्द्राविष्णु सह स्तुतौ | गृहाणि वा वैष्णवानि ता वामित्यृचि काङ्क्षति ||

4.s: jīrṇaṃ tu dīrghatamasaṃ khinnāstatparicāriṇaḥ | dāsā baddhvā nadītoye dṛṣṭihīnamavādadhuḥ ||
4.d: जीर्णं तु दीर्घतमसं खिन्नास्तत्परिचारिणः | दासा बद्ध्वा नदीतोये दृष्टिहीनमवादधुः ||

4.s: tatraikastraitano nāma śastreṇainamapāhanat | śiraścāṃsāvuraścaiva svayameva nyakṛntata ||
4.d: तत्रैकस्त्रैतनो नाम शस्त्रेणैनमपाहनत् | शिरश्चांसावुरश्चैव स्वयमेव न्यकृन्तत ||
4.e: One among them, Traitana by name, tried to strike him away with his sword, and (in so doing) cut to pieces (nyakrntata) his own head, shoulders and breast. i.

4.s: hatvā dīrghatamāstaṃ tu pāpena mahatā vṛtama | ātmāṅgānyanudaccaiva tatrodonmohnito bhṛśam ||
4.d: हत्वा दीर्घतमास्तं तु पापेन महता वृतम | आत्माङ्गान्यनुदच्चैव तत्रोदोन्मोह्नितो भृशम् ||
4.e: Now Dirghatamas having (thus) slain him (who had) involved (himself) in great sin, moved his limbs there (in the river), (though) excessively stupefied (unmohita) by the water (uda).

4.s: aṅgadeśasamīpe tu taṃ nadyaḥ samudakṣipan | aṅgarājagṛhe yuktām uśijaṃ putrakāmyayā ||
4.d: अङ्गदेशसमीपे तु तं नद्यः समुदक्षिपन् | अङ्गराजगृहे युक्ताम् उशिजं पुत्रकाम्यया ||
4.e: Now the currents (nadyah) a threw him up in the neighbourhood of the Anga country. B Usij was employed b in the house of the king of Anga.

4.s: rājñā ca prahitāṃ dāsīṃ bhaktāṃ matvā mahātapāḥ | janayāmāsa cotthāya kakṣīvatpramukhānṛṣīn ||
4.d: राज्ञा च प्रहितां दासीं भक्तां मत्वा महातपाः | जनयामास चोत्थाय कक्षीवत्प्रमुखानृषीन् ||

4.s: tuṣṭāva caiva sūktābhyām abodhītyaśvināvṛṣiḥ | preti dyāvāpṛthivyau tu parābhyāmetaduttaram ||
4.d: तुष्टाव चैव सूक्ताभ्याम् अबोधीत्यश्विनावृषिः | प्रेति द्यावापृथिव्यौ तु पराभ्यामेतदुत्तरम् ||

4.s: kimārbhavaṃ pare mā no medhyasyāśvasya saṃstavaḥ | īrmāntāsa iti tvasyāṃ nīyamānaṃ praśaṃsati ||
4.d: किमार्भवं परे मा नो मेध्यस्याश्वस्य संस्तवः | ईर्मान्तास इति त्वस्यां नीयमानं प्रशंसति ||
4.e: (beginning) 'Why' (kim: i. 161. 1) is addressed to the Rbhus. The two (162, 163) following (beginning) 'Not us (ma nah i. 162. 1) are a laudation of the sacrificial horse. In the (stanza) Full-haunched' (irmantasah: i. 163. 10) he extols the horse as he is being led.

4.s: svayūthyāstasya caivātra bahavaḥ saṃstutā hayāḥ | niyuktāścāniyuktāśca prasaṅgādanukīrtitāḥ ||
4.d: स्वयूथ्यास्तस्य चैवात्र बहवः संस्तुता हयाः | नियुक्ताश्चानियुक्ताश्च प्रसङ्गादनुकीर्तिताः ||
4.e: And here also (i. 163. 10) the many steeds belonging to his troop (svayuthyah) are praised: both the yoked and unyoked are incidentally (prasangat) mentioned.

4.s: saṃjñaptavadasaṃjñaptaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ cāha bhūtavat | tasya māṃsasya sūnasya carūṇāṃ haviṣastathā ||
4.d: संज्ञप्तवदसंज्ञप्तं भविष्यं चाह भूतवत् | तस्य मांसस्य सूनस्य चरूणां हविषस्तथा ||
4.e: He speaks of him (though) not (yet) sacrificed as (already) sacrificed, of (his) future (state) as if past. Of his flesh (mamsa), of the basket (suna), of the pots (caru), and of the oblation (havis)

4.s: vāso'dhivāsasoścātra yadviśasyaṃ ca kīrtitam | gātrasya śūlasthūṇānāṃ svadhiteśca prakīrtanam ||
4.d: वासोऽधिवाससोश्चात्र यद्विशस्यं च कीर्तितम् | गात्रस्य शूलस्थूणानां स्वधितेश्च प्रकीर्तनम् ||

4.s: chāgasya kīrtanaṃ cātra indrāpūṣṇoḥ saha stutiḥ | sūktaṃ yadasyavāmīyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ taducyate ||
4.d: छागस्य कीर्तनं चात्र इन्द्रापूष्णोः सह स्तुतिः | सूक्तं यदस्यवामीयं वैश्वदेवं तदुच्यते ||
4.e: There is here also mention of the goat (chaga) (and) praise at the same time of Indra-Pusan. " The hymn which (begins) Of this benignant' (asya vamasya: i. 164) c is stated to be addressed to the All-gods. chagasya hm'rbfkrº, bhagasya r.

4.s: pravādā vidhidhāstatra devānāṃ cātra kīrtanam | sūkte'syarci parokṣoktā vakṣyāmi bhrātarastrayaḥ ||
4.d: प्रवादा विधिधास्तत्र देवानां चात्र कीर्तनम् | सूक्तेऽस्यर्चि परोक्षोक्ता वक्ष्यामि भ्रातरस्त्रयः ||
4.e: In it are various sayings (pravadah) and here (too) mention of the gods. B In the stanza 'Of this' (asya: i. 164. 1) in the hymn, three brothers a are spoken of in the third person (paroksa)-I will explain (them). 134 tatra, tvatra r, vatra h.

4.s: agnistu vāmaḥ palito vāyurbhrātā tu madhyamaḥ | ghṛtapṛṣṭhastṛtīyo'tra sapta vai raśmaya stutāḥ ||
4.d: अग्निस्तु वामः पलितो वायुर्भ्राता तु मध्यमः | घृतपृष्ठस्तृतीयोऽत्र सप्त वै रश्मय स्तुताः ||
4.e: Now the benignant, grey-haired one is Agni, while the middle brother is Vayu. The third here is butter-backed (ghrtaprstha) (his) seven rays are praised.

4.s: parāstu kathayantyagniṃ yathā varṣati pāti ca | ahorātrāndinānmāsān ṛtūṃśca parivartinaḥ ||
4.d: परास्तु कथयन्त्यग्निं यथा वर्षति पाति च | अहोरात्रान्दिनान्मासान् ऋतूंश्च परिवर्तिनः ||
4.e: But the following (stanzas) tell of Agni, how he rains and protects; and of days and nights (ahoratra), of days (dina), of months, and of revolving seasons.

4.s: pañcadhā ca tridhā caiva ṣoḍhā dvādaśadhaiva ca | saṃvatsaraṃ cakravacca parābhiḥ kīrtayatyṛṣiḥ ||
4.d: पञ्चधा च त्रिधा चैव षोढा द्वादशधैव च | संवत्सरं चक्रवच्च पराभिः कीर्तयत्यृषिः ||
4.e: With the following (stanzas) a the seer celebrates the year (samvatsara) like a wheel (as) fivefold, and threefold, sixfold and twelvefold;

4.s: kṣetrajñānaṃ ca dhenuṃ ca gaurīṃ vācaṃ sarasvatīm | dharmaṃ pūrvayugīyaṃ ca sādhyāndevagaṇāṃstathā ||
4.d: क्षेत्रज्ञानं च धेनुं च गौरीं वाचं सरस्वतीम् | धर्मं पूर्वयुगीयं च साध्यान्देवगणांस्तथा ||

4.s: vividhāni ca karmāṇi agnivāyuvivasvatām | vibhūtimagnervāyośca jagati sthāsnujaṅgame ||
4.d: विविधानि च कर्माणि अग्निवायुविवस्वताम् | विभूतिमग्नेर्वायोश्च जगति स्थास्नुजङ्गमे ||

4.s: haraṇaṃ raśmibhirvāro visargaṃ punareva ca | karmānukīrtanaṃ cātra parjanyāgnivivasvatām ||

4.e: The body joined with the organs of sense is designated ksetra. Prana alone knows it: hence he (Prana) is spoken of as 'he who knows the body' (ksetra-jna).

4.e: Saka is (used) in (the sense of) cloud; its dhuma is water b or garment. The bull d is Soma; and the three lords e (adhipa) are his purifiers f.

4.e: That (part of i. 164) which ends with (the stanza) 'The buffalo' (gaurih: i. 164. 41) is addressed to the All-gods; afterwards there may be (said to be) separate praise (prthak-stuti). The two (stanzas: 46, 47), 'Indra, Mitra' (indram mitram: i. 164. 46), are addressed to Surya; the last (stanza) to Sarasvat (i. 164.52). may optionally (va) be addressed to Surya.

4.e: A story of ancient events (puravrtta) is (here) proclaimed by the seers. Satakratu (Indra), while roaming in the sky, fell in with the Maruts.

4.e: On seeing them Indra praised them, and they as seers addressed Indra. By the aid of austerity Agastya became fully (tattvatah) aware of their dialogue.

4.e: This choice (made by Grtsamada) is explained in the final (6) stanza (of Rg-veda ii. 21), 'O Indra, the best' (indra sresthani): he chose all this as a boon. The Lord of Saci hearing that,

4.s: tathetyuktvā turāṣāṭ tu pāṇau jagrāha dakṣiṇe | ṛṣiścāsya sakhitvena pāṇinā pāṇimaspṛśat ||
4.d: तथेत्युक्त्वा तुराषाट् तु पाणौ जग्राह दक्षिणे | ऋषिश्चास्य सखित्वेन पाणिना पाणिमस्पृशत् ||

4.s: sahitau jagmatuścaivaṃ mahendrasadanaṃ prati | tatrainamārhayatprītyā svayameva puraṃdaraḥ ||
4.d: सहितौ जग्मतुश्चैवं महेन्द्रसदनं प्रति | तत्रैनमार्हयत्प्रीत्या स्वयमेव पुरंदरः ||
4.e: And thus they went together to great Indra's abode. There the Destroyer of Forts (puramdara) himself affectionately honoured him,

4.s: karmaṇā vidhidṛṣṭena tamṛṣiṃ cābhyapūjayat | sakhitvācca punaścainam uvāca harivāhanaḥ ||
4.d: कर्मणा विधिदृष्टेन तमृषिं चाभ्यपूजयत् | सखित्वाच्च पुनश्चैनम् उवाच हरिवाहनः ||

4.s: gṛṇanmādayase yasmāt tvamasmānṛṣisattama | tasmādgṛtsamado nāma śaunahotro bhaviṣyasi ||
4.d: गृणन्मादयसे यस्मात् त्वमस्मानृषिसत्तम | तस्माद्गृत्समदो नाम शौनहोत्रो भविष्यसि ||
4.e: 'Since you, O best of seers, with your praise (grnan) a delight (madayase) us, therefore, being the son of Sunahotra, you shall be (called) Grtsamada by name.

4.s: tato dvādaśabhiḥ sūktais tuṣṭāvendraṃ śrudhītyṛṣiḥ | dadarśa saṃstuvanneva tatra sa brahmaṇaspatim ||
4.d: ततो द्वादशभिः सूक्तैस् तुष्टावेन्द्रं श्रुधीत्यृषिः | ददर्श संस्तुवन्नेव तत्र स ब्रह्मणस्पतिम् ||
4.e: Then with the twelve (ii. 11-22) hymns (beginning) 'Hear' (srudhi ii. 11. 1) the seer praised Indra. And just as he was praising (him) he saw Brahmanaspati there.

4.s: bṛhaspatiṃ tu tuṣṭāva dṛṣṭaliṅgābhireva ca | sa tamapyabhituṣṭāva caturbhirita uttaraiḥ ||
4.d: बृहस्पतिं तु तुष्टाव दृष्टलिङ्गाभिरेव च | स तमप्यभितुष्टाव चतुर्भिरित उत्तरैः ||
4.e: Now he praised Brhaspati also in those (stanzas) in which (that form of) the name (linga) a appears. He praised him also b with the four (hymns) after this (ii. 23-26)

4.s: gaṇānāṃ viśvamityasyāṃ sahendrābrāhmaṇaspatī | bṛhaspatiṃ prasaṅgādvā brahmaṇaspatimeva ca ||
4.d: गणानां विश्वमित्यस्यां सहेन्द्राब्राह्मणस्पती | बृहस्पतिं प्रसङ्गाद्वा ब्रह्मणस्पतिमेव च ||
4.e: (beginning) 'Of the hosts' (gananam: ii. 23. 1); in the All' (visvam ii. 24. 12) Indra and Brahmanaspati Ora (he praised) Brhaspati incidentally (prasangat) and Brahmanaspati strictly speaking (eva). (stanza) together.

4.s: tuṣṭāva karmaṇaikena prabhāvasyāntaraṃ dvayoḥ | mitrāvaruṇadakṣāṃśātuvijātabhagāryamṇām ||
4.d: तुष्टाव कर्मणैकेन प्रभावस्यान्तरं द्वयोः | मित्रावरुणदक्षांशातुविजातभगार्यम्णाम् ||
4.e: He praised the different power of the two by (lauding) one and the same deed. To Mitra, Varuna, Daksa, Amsa, Tuvijata, Bhaga,

4.s: ādityānāmimāḥ sūktam idaṃ vāruṇamucyate | vāruṇī yo ma ityādyā duḥsvapnādyapraṇāśinī ||
4.d: आदित्यानामिमाः सूक्तम् इदं वारुणमुच्यते | वारुणी यो म इत्याद्या दुःस्वप्नाद्यप्रणाशिनी ||

4.s: dhṛtavratā vaiśvadevam śatamaindraṃ paraṃ tu yat | pra hi kratumiti tvasyām indrāsomau saha stutau ||
4.d: धृतव्रता वैश्वदेवम् शतमैन्द्रं परं तु यत् | प्र हि क्रतुमिति त्वस्याम् इन्द्रासोमौ सह स्तुतौ ||
4.e: 'Upholders of law' (dhrtavratah: ii. 29) is addressed to the All-gods, but that which follows, 'Right' (rtam: ii. 30), is addressed to Indra. In the (stanza) His power indeed' (pra hi kratum ii. 30. 6) Indra-Soma are praised together. " param tu yat

4.s: sarasvatī tvamityasminn ardharcaṃ madhyamā tu vāk | bṛhaspatistutiryo nas taṃ va ṛṅ marutāṃ stutiḥ ||
4.d: सरस्वती त्वमित्यस्मिन्न् अर्धर्चं मध्यमा तु वाक् | बृहस्पतिस्तुतिर्यो नस् तं व ऋङ् मरुतां स्तुतिः ||
4.e: But in the hemistich 'O Sarasvati, thou' (Sarasvati tvam: ii. 30. 8) the Middle Vac (is praised). 'Who us' (yo nah: ii. 30. 9) is (in) praise of Brhaspati; the stanza 'That of yours' (tam vah: ii. 30. 11) is (in) praise of the Maruts.

4.s: asmākaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ syād ādāvasyeti cāsya ṛk | dyāvāpṛthivyostvāṣṭryau vā athavaindryau pare tataḥ ||
4.d: अस्माकं वैश्वदेवं स्याद् आदावस्येति चास्य ऋक् | द्यावापृथिव्योस्त्वाष्ट्र्यौ वा अथवैन्द्र्यौ परे ततः ||
4.e: 'Our' (asmakam: ii. 31) should be (regarded as) addressed to the All-gods; and the stanza at the beginning of (the hymn) Of this' (asya: ii. 32. 1) belongs to Heaven and Earth; the two following it (ii. 32. 2, 3) are addressed either to Tvastr or to Indra.

4.s: dve dvai rākāsinovālyoḥ ṣaḍ guṅgvādyāstathāntyayā | tatpūrvaṃ dve ṛcau kuhvāḥ kuhūmahamiti smṛte ||
4.d: द्वे द्वै राकासिनोवाल्योः षड् गुङ्ग्वाद्यास्तथान्त्यया | तत्पूर्वं द्वे ऋचौ कुह्वाः कुहूमहमिति स्मृते ||
4.e: Two (stanzas) each belong to Raka (ii. 32.4, 5 ) and Sinivali (6, 7), while with the last (8) the six ( goddesses) Gungu and the rest (are praised) : B preceded by these (stanzas: tatpurve) there are two stanzas (beginning) 'Kuhu I' & (kuhum aham) traditionally held (to belong) to Kuhu. sat gungadyas, sad

4.s: taduttare dve'numataira anu no'nviditi smṛte | dhātuścatasrastatrādo dhātā dadātu no rayim ||
4.d: तदुत्तरे द्वेऽनुमतैर अनु नोऽन्विदिति स्मृते | धातुश्चतस्रस्तत्रादो धाता ददातु नो रयिम् ||
4.e: Followed by these (taduttare) there are two, anu nah (and) anv it, traditionally held to belong to Anumati. At the beginning in the same place there are four ( stanzas) to Dhatr (beginning) - May the Creator grant us wealth' (dhata dadatu no rajim ).

4.s: raudraṃ mārutaṃ tu praram ā te dhārāvarā iti | vāmatastu mṛgaṃ dṛṣṭvā bibhyadetya ṛṣiḥ svayam ||
4.d: रौद्रं मारुतं तु प्ररम् आ ते धारावरा इति | वामतस्तु मृगं दृष्ट्वा बिभ्यदेत्य ऋषिः स्वयम् ||

4.s: stuhi śrutamiti tvasyāṃ tamevāstautprasādayan | apāṃ napādupetyatra stutaḥ sūkte tataḥ pare ||
4.d: स्तुहि श्रुतमिति त्वस्यां तमेवास्तौत्प्रसादयन् | अपां नपादुपेत्यत्र स्तुतः सूक्ते ततः परे ||

4.s: tubhyamityārtave sūktaṃ sāvitrādāśvinaṃ param | somaḥ pūṣāditiścaiva somapauṣṇe'ntyayā stutāḥ ||
4.d: तुभ्यमित्यार्तवे सूक्तं सावित्रादाश्विनं परम् | सोमः पूषादितिश्चैव सोमपौष्णेऽन्त्यया स्तुताः ||
4.e: There are two hymns (ii. 36, 37) addressed to the Seasons (beginning) To thee' (tubhyam: ii. 36. 1). After one addressed to Savitr (38) follows one to the Asvins (39). With the last (stanza: 6) of (the hymn) to Soma-Pusan (40), Soma, Pusan, and Aditi as well, are praised.

4.s: vāyavye caindravāyavī pañcātha prāugāstṛcāḥ | pretyṛkstauti havirdhāne agnistatra nipātabhāk | dyāvāpṛthivyau dyāveti havirdhāne tataḥ pare ||
4.d: वायव्ये चैन्द्रवायवी पञ्चाथ प्राउगास्तृचाः | प्रेत्यृक्स्तौति हविर्धाने अग्निस्तत्र निपातभाक् | द्यावापृथिव्यौ द्यावेति हविर्धाने ततः परे ||
4.e: And (at the beginning of ii. 41) there are two (stanzas) to Vayu (1, 2), one to Indra -Vayu (3); next (come) five triplets (4-18) addressed to the Prauga deities. The stanza Forth' (pra: 19) praises the two Soma carts: Agni is there incidental (nipata-bhaj). Heaven and Earth' (dyava: 20) (praises) Heaven and Earth; then follow (21) the two Soma carts. 4.d: स्तुतिं तु पुनरेवेच्छन्न् इन्द्रो भूत्वा कपिञ्जलः | ऋषेर्जिगमिषोराशां ववाशास्थाय दक्षिणाम् ||
4.e: Now

4.s: sa tamārṣeṇa saṃprekṣya cakṣuṣā pakṣirūpiṇam | parābhyāmabhituṣṭāva sūktābhyāṃ tu kanikradat ||
4.d: स तमार्षेण संप्रेक्ष्य चक्षुषा पक्षिरूपिणम् | पराभ्यामभितुष्टाव सूक्ताभ्यां तु कनिक्रदत् ||
4.e: He (Grtsamada), with the eye of a seer, recognizing him (Indra) in the form of the bird, praised him in the two following hymns (ii. 42, 43), 'With repeated cry' (kanikradat: ii. 42. 1).

4.s: praśāsya gāṃ yastapasābhyagacchad brahmarṣitāmekaśataṃ ca putrān | sa gathiputrastu jagāda sūktaṃ somasya metyāgneyaṃ yatpare ca ||
4.d: प्रशास्य गां यस्तपसाभ्यगच्छद् ब्रह्मर्षितामेकशतं च पुत्रान् | स गथिपुत्रस्तु जगाद सूक्तं सोमस्य मेत्याग्नेयं यत्परे च ||

4.s: vaiśvānarīye samitsamidāpryo dve āgneye uttare tvatra sūkte | dyāvāpṛthivyā uṣaso nipātā āpo'tha devāḥ pitaraśca mitraḥ ||
4.d: वैश्वानरीये समित्समिदाप्र्यो द्वे आग्नेये उत्तरे त्वत्र सूक्ते | द्यावापृथिव्या उषसो निपाता आपोऽथ देवाः पितरश्च मित्रः ||

4.s: āgneyeṣu dṛśyante stutāstu vaiśvānaro varuṇo jātavedāḥ | stuyetaikā yatra yatrāstutirvā nipātyarthāṃścopamārthāṃśca vidyāt ||
4.d: आग्नेयेषु दृश्यन्ते स्तुतास्तु वैश्वानरो वरुणो जातवेदाः | स्तुयेतैका यत्र यत्रास्तुतिर्वा निपात्यर्थांश्चोपमार्थांश्च विद्यात् ||
4.e: In (hymns) addressed to Agni, Vaisvanara, Varuna, Jatavedas are seen to be praised. Wherever (here) one (of them) may be praised or there is no (actual) praise, one should know that they are intended to be incidental or to serve as a comparison. stu

4.s: rājarṣayo gṛtsamadā vasiṣṭhā bharadvājāḥ kuśikā gotamāśca | viśve'śvināvaṅgiraso'trayo'ditir bhojāḥ kaṇvā bhṛgavo rodasī diśaḥ ||
4.d: राजर्षयो गृत्समदा वसिष्ठा भरद्वाजाः कुशिका गोतमाश्च | विश्वेऽश्विनावङ्गिरसोऽत्रयोऽदितिर् भोजाः कण्वा भृगवो रोदसी दिशः ||
4.e: The royal seers, the Grtsamadas, the Vasisthas, the Bharadvajas, the Kusikas, and the Gotamas, the All (gods), the Asvins, the Angirases, the Atris, Aditi, the Bhojas, the Kanvas, the Bhrgus, the Two Worlds (rodasi), the Regions (disah)

4.s: sāvitrasaubhyāśvinamāruteṣu aindrāgneye raudrasauryauṣaseṣu | ādāvante saktamadhye stutāstu na vyāghnanti devatāḥ sūktabhājaḥ ||
4.d: सावित्रसौभ्याश्विनमारुतेषु ऐन्द्राग्नेये रौद्रसौर्यौषसेषु | आदावन्ते सक्तमध्ये स्तुतास्तु न व्याघ्नन्ति देवताः सूक्तभाजः ||

4.s: agneḥ saptadaśo'dhyāya ūrdhvaṃ ū ṣu ṇa ūtaye | ete kāṇvyāvṛcau yaupyāv añjanti pañca ca ||
4.d: अग्नेः सप्तदशोऽध्याय ऊर्ध्वं ऊ षु ण ऊतये | एते काण्व्यावृचौ यौप्याव् अञ्जन्ति पञ्च च ||
4.e: The seventeenth Adhyaya (Rg-veda iii. 7-29) is Agni's. Stand erect to aid us' (urdhva u su na utaye: i. 36. 13, 14)these two stanzas of Kanva are addressed to the sacrificial post (yaupi), and the five (beginning) They anoint thee' (anjanti tvaa: iii. 8. 1-5).

4.s: śeṣā bahubhyo yūpebhyo vaiśvadevī tvṛgaṣṭamī | asyāntyā vraścanā yoktā ṣaṣṭhamaindrāgnamucyate ||
4.d: शेषा बहुभ्यो यूपेभ्यो वैश्वदेवी त्वृगष्टमी | अस्यान्त्या व्रश्चना योक्ता षष्ठमैन्द्राग्नमुच्यते ||
4.e: The resta (are addressed) to many posts, while the eighth stanza is addressed to the All-gods; the last (stanza) of this (hymn) is that which is said to be concerned with cutting (the post). The sixth (hymn: iii. 12) c is said to be addressed to Indra-Agni.

4.s: agnimuṣasaṃ vaiśvadevo dadhikrāmiti caitayā | āgnendrī tvagna indraścark paro vaiśvānarastṛcaḥ ||
4.d: अग्निमुषसं वैश्वदेवो दधिक्रामिति चैतया | आग्नेन्द्री त्वग्न इन्द्रश्चर्क् परो वैश्वानरस्तृचः ||
4.e: (The stanza) 'Agni, Dawn' (agnim usasam: iii. 20. 1) is addressed to the All-gods; (they are) also (invoked) with the (stanza) 'Dadhikra' (dadhikram: iii. 20. 5). But the stanza 'Agni and Indra' (agna indras ca iii. 25. 4) is addressed to Agni-Indra. The following triplet (iii. 26. 1-3) is addressed to Vaisvanara. II.

4.s: pra yantu mārutañcāntyā śatadhāraṃ gurustavaḥ | pra vo vājā ṛtūnstauti ṛtvija stauti manthata ||
4.d: प्र यन्तु मारुतञ्चान्त्या शतधारं गुरुस्तवः | प्र वो वाजा ऋतून्स्तौति ऋत्विज स्तौति मन्थत ||
4.e: And (the triplet) Let them go forth' (pra yantu: iii. 26. 4-6) is addressed to the Maruts. The last (stanza), 'With a hundred streams' (Satadharam: iii. 26. 9), is (in) praise of a preceptor. 'Forth your food' (pra vo vajah: iii. 27. 1) praises the seasons; 'Rub ye' (manthata: iii. 29. 5) praises the priests.

4.s: puroṣyāsa iti tvasyāṃ dhiṣṇyānagnīnpraśaṃsati | jñeyāścaiva tu hotāram te daivyāścaiva tatra tu ||
4.d: पुरोष्यास इति त्वस्यां धिष्ण्यानग्नीन्प्रशंसति | ज्ञेयाश्चैव तु होतारम् ते दैव्याश्चैव तत्र तु ||
4.e: But in the (stanza) 'Misty' (purisyasah: iii. 22. 4) he (the seer) lauds the fires on the altar (dhisnya). Now they are there to be recognized as the Divine Sacrificers.

4.s: trayoviṃśatiraindrāṇi icchantīti parāṇyataḥ | sūkte preti tu nadyaśca viśvāmitraḥ samūdire ||
4.d: त्रयोविंशतिरैन्द्राणि इच्छन्तीति पराण्यतः | सूक्ते प्रेति तु नद्यश्च विश्वामित्रः समूदिरे ||
4.e: The twenty-three (hymns) after this (beginning) 'They desire' (ichanti: iii. 30) are addressed to Indra. But in the hymn Forth' (pra: iii. 33) Visvamitra and the Rivers engaged in a dialogue.

4.s: purohitaḥ sannijyārthaṃ sudāsā saha yannṛṣiḥ | vipāṭchutudrayoḥ saṃbhedaṃ śamityete uvāca ha ||
4.d: पुरोहितः सन्निज्यार्थं सुदासा सह यन्नृषिः | विपाट्छुतुद्रयोः संभेदं शमित्येते उवाच ह ||
4.e: The seer going with Sudas-being his domestic priest for the sake of sacrifice-to the confluence of the Vipas and the Sutudri addressed these two (rivers) with (the words) 'Be propitious' (sam). iii.

4.s: pravādāstatra dṛśyante dvivadbahuvadekavat | acchetyardharce paccho vā nadīṣvapyekavanni te ||
4.d: प्रवादास्तत्र दृश्यन्ते द्विवद्बहुवदेकवत् | अच्छेत्यर्धर्चे पच्छो वा नदीष्वप्येकवन्नि ते ||
4.e: In that (hymn) there appear statements (pravadah) in the dual, plurala, and singular in the hemistich 'Unto' (acha: iii. 33. 3) or in the (successive) padas (pacchah) 'Down to thee' (ni te: 10°, 10, 11), in the singular (ekavat) in (reference to) the

4.s: ādye dvṛce dvivatsārdhe viśvāmitravacaḥ śruteḥ | etābhirṛgbhirvā nadya ṛṣi bahuvadūcire ||
